name: 1400 Bar & Grill
description: 1400 Bar & Grill is a casual gastropub at the corner of Webster Street and Central Avenue in Alameda's West End. It fills the ground floor of the historic Croll Building, built in 1879. The building once housed Croll's Gardens and Hotel, where boxing greats such as James J. Corbett and Jack Johnson trained around the turn of the 20th century. It is now a California Historical Landmark, and the restaurant keeps its stained glass, etched windows and carved wooden bar. The kitchen serves pub fare drawn from a range of culinary traditions, with daily specials and pizza. Takeout and delivery are available.

name: A-Town Pizza and Kabob House
description: A-Town Pizza and Kabob House has been a neighborhood fixture on Blanding Avenue since the late 1980s. It serves two cuisines: American-style gourmet pizza on dough made fresh every day, and Afghan kabobs char-broiled after marinating in house seasoning. Pizza favorites include the loaded A-Town Special and a gourmet veggie pie. On the kabob side there are chopan (lamb chop), tekah (beef) and chicken kabobs. Halal pizzas, pastas and kabobs make it a good choice for families with a range of dietary needs. The shop is open seven days a week for dine-in, pickup and delivery.

name: Abigail's Moroccan Cuisine
description: Abigail's Moroccan Cuisine is a family-run restaurant on Ballena Isle with views over San Francisco Bay. Jonathan and Fatima Belkhalfia opened it in 2010 and named it after their daughter. The menu offers home-style Moroccan cooking, including kefta sandwiches, harira and lentil soups, saffron rice plates, Moroccan salads, and slow-cooked tagines such as lamb with almonds and dried plums or chicken with green olives and preserved lemon. Saturday dinners are a highlight, with belly dancing entertainment. Guests may bring their own wine. Lunch is served most days and dinner on weekends.

name: Alameda Brewing
description: Alameda Brewing is a family-owned craft brewery and taproom on Park Street in downtown Alameda. Founder Bill Phua and his son Vince run it. It opened as Alameda Island Brewing Company and, in 2024, took back the name it had always intended, with a new nautical rope "A" logo and a refreshed taproom. The rotating lineup runs from West Coast and hazy IPAs to a Czech pilsner, German lager, hefeweizen and a playful ube ale, plus hard seltzer and non-alcoholic options. There is no kitchen, but guests may bring food or order from neighboring restaurants on the shared patio. Kids with adults and leashed dogs are welcome, and the calendar includes live music, trivia and comedy.

name: Alameda Cinema Grill
description: Alameda Cinema Grill is a neighborhood restaurant and bar inside the Alameda Theatres Cineplex on Central Avenue. Its "backstage pass" corridor connects directly to the cinema, so guests can have dinner and then take their food and drinks into the movie. The kitchen serves eclectic comfort food. The bar pours craft cocktails inspired by Hollywood's Golden Age, alongside beer and wine. Weekend brunch, regular live music, and Wednesday comedy and karaoke nights make it a lively spot even without a film. For celebrations, the restaurant offers party packages, including options that pair a private theater rental with a full meal.

name: Alley & Vine
description: Alley & Vine is a New American restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. It serves seasonal dishes, freshly baked breads and handcrafted cocktails in a warm neighborhood setting. The menu leans toward seafood and chophouse favorites such as king salmon, branzino, seafood risotto, lamb chops and filet mignon, with house focaccia on the side. Daytime diners will find dishes like ham benedict. The restaurant is open daily from late morning through dinner, takes reservations, and handles private parties and catering.

name: Ark Chinese Restaurant
description: Ark Chinese Restaurant is a casual Park Street spot best known for hand-pulled noodles, which are made fresh in the kitchen and served in hearty noodle soups and lo mein dishes. The broad menu of traditional Chinese dishes covers beef, chicken, pork and vegetarian options, along with favorites like xiao long bao and golden braised egg tofu. Big round tables make it a natural choice for family dinners and group meals, and it is also a regular weekday lunch stop. Takeout and delivery are available.

name: Asena Restaurant
description: Asena Restaurant has served Mediterranean cooking on Santa Clara Avenue in downtown Alameda since 1996. Owners Mustafa Yildirim and Muhittin Arpaci grew up in kitchens where their mothers cured olives and baked bread, and they bring that from-scratch approach to Asena. The kitchen bakes its own bread, rolls fresh pasta, cures salmon and preserves lemons in house. It sources fresh, seasonal, local and organic ingredients wherever possible. Asena is open for dinner Monday through Saturday, offers catering, and has long supported Alameda schools and charities.

name: Bhan Mae Vane
description: Bhan Mae Vane is a modern Lao and Thai restaurant on Webster Street in Alameda's West End, run by sisters Bebe Lach, the chef, and Thip Tran. Their mother's recipes inspire the menu, which updates traditional dishes with local, seasonal ingredients. The cooking features the bold spice, funk and earthy bitterness at the heart of Lao and Thai food, in dishes like crispy pork belly, slow-simmered red curry, and tapioca dumplings filled with pork and peanuts. The dining room is casual and lively, well suited to big groups. Lunch and dinner are served Tuesday through Sunday, and takeout is available.

name: Burma Superstar
description: Burma Superstar brings Burmese cooking to Park Street in downtown Alameda, where it has served the neighborhood since 2008 as part of a Bay Area brand dating to 1992. The kitchen draws on a cuisine shaped by India, China, Laos and Thailand. Its best-known dish is the tea leaf salad of fermented tea leaves, vegetables and crunchy nuts. Samusa soup, flaky platha flatbread, khao swè curry noodles and beef curry are also favorites. The warm, neighborhood-style dining room suits first-time visitors and family dinners alike. Reservations are available, and the restaurant also offers online pickup ordering, catering and gift cards. Open daily for lunch and dinner.

name: C'era Una Volta
description: C'era Una Volta ("once upon a time") has been cooking Tuscan-style Italian food in Alameda since 2004. Chef Rutilio "Rudy" Fanetti-Durán and Cheryl Principato founded it. Today the kitchen operates inside the SoFive Soccer Club at Alameda Point, focusing on carryout, delivery and catering, with indoor and outdoor seating. The menu features house-made pasta, pizza and salads, seasonal dishes, vegetarian and vegan options, and weekly Tuesday specials. It also caters corporate events and parties and delivers to nearby wineries. Honors include repeated recognition from the Accademia Italiana della Cucina and a Best of Alameda 2025 award.

name: Cafe Jolie
description: Cafe Jolie is a French-inspired neighborhood restaurant on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. It focuses on organic, seasonal cooking led by Executive Chef Joann Guitarte. Diners know it for breakfast and weekend brunch, and the menu also includes French-American plates such as steak frites, Dungeness crab cocktail and beignets. Beer and wine are served, gluten-free options are available, and there is patio seating outdoors. Live jazz on Friday and Saturday evenings adds to the relaxed, welcoming feel. Takeout is available, and a public parking lot sits next door.

name: Calafia Taqueria
description: Calafia Taqueria has served fresh, traditional Mexican food on Webster Street in Alameda's West End for more than two decades. The menu is built around taqueria staples with a wide choice of fillings: carne asada, pollo asado, carnitas, chile verde, lengua, al pastor, shredded chicken, fish and shrimp. Guests can eat in, order ahead online for pickup, or use the free parking next to the restaurant. Calafia also caters parties and community events around the island, and its patio is available to rent for gatherings.

name: Casa Revolución Taqueria
description: Casa Revolución Taqueria serves fresh, fairly priced Mexican food on Santa Clara Avenue near downtown Alameda. The menu covers breakfast, lunch and dinner. Corn tortillas are made by hand, and the salsa bar lets diners dress their tacos as they like. Birria is a house specialty, and tacos anchor the menu. The taqueria offers dine-in, takeout and online ordering for pickup or delivery, and it can cater gatherings with buffet-style spreads. With early weekend openings, it works for a morning breakfast burrito as well as an evening taco run.

name: Ceron Kitchen
description: Ceron Kitchen opened on Webster Street in Alameda's West End in October 2021. Owner Vicente Ceron, who founded it with Executive Chef Juan Jaquez, had long dreamed of opening a restaurant. Chef Jaquez cooks New American food with careful plating and deep flavors. Dishes include New Zealand lamb, duck breast, seafood pasta, ribeye with bleu cheese and clam chowder, alongside craft cocktails. Complimentary pastries often close the meal. The restaurant is open daily for lunch and dinner, takes reservations, and hosts private parties and catering. It received an OpenTable Diners' Choice award in 2025, and free parking is available nearby.

name: Cholita Linda
description: Cholita Linda brings Latin street and comfort food to Park Street in downtown Alameda. It is the second location of the Oakland favorite that chef Vanessa Chavez and her husband Murat Sozeri grew from popular farmers market stands. Chavez's Peruvian, Chinese, Cuban and Mexican heritage shapes the menu. The Baja fish taco is the star: lightly battered fish with slaw, crema, radish and lime on corn tortillas. Chicharrón de pollo, Cubano sandwiches and yuca fries with ají amarillo round out the menu. Ordering is fast-casual in a bright, tropical-themed space. Catering and online ordering are also available.

name: Domenico's Italian Deli
description: Domenico's Italian Deli is a three-generation family institution on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. Its roots go back to 1966, when Dominic "Domenico" Cucchiara and his Italian-born wife Letizia bought the P&G Italian Delicatessen. The shop took the name Domenico's in 1982, and their daughter Ann Murphy has run it since 1989, with the next generation working behind the counter. The deli makes around 40 sandwiches with house-roasted turkey, hot coppa and hand-rolled meatballs. It also offers made-to-order pasta, and cannoli and cheesecake from family recipes. Open Monday through Saturday.

name: Dragon Rouge Bistro
description: Dragon Rouge Bistro is a waterfront Vietnamese restaurant on Blanding Avenue, along Alameda's northern shoreline. Its contemporary dining room and outdoor seating look out toward the bridge. Favorites include garlic noodles, "bouncing" beef tenderloin, pineapple fried rice and a crispy dragon's nest with prawns. The full bar pours craft cocktails, and daily happy hour pricing makes it a lively after-work stop. The restaurant is open every day for lunch and dinner, and also offers private dining, catering, takeout and delivery.

name: East End
description: East End is an independent, locally owned restaurant inside The Marketplace on Park Street. Since 2011 it has made wood-fired pizza from a native-yeast sourdough, and the menu has since grown to include oysters shucked to order, craft cocktails and seasonal comfort dishes. The kitchen buys from local, responsible producers. East End serves dinner Tuesday through Saturday. Its daily 5–6 pm happy hour takes a dollar off house cocktails, draft beer and wine, and offers a dozen oysters for $12. Guests can dine in, order ahead for pickup, or get delivery.

name: East Ocean Seafood Restaurant
description: East Ocean Seafood Restaurant on Webster Street has been a gathering place for the East Bay community for more than thirty years. The Cantonese-style restaurant serves dim sum at midday every day and Chinese seafood dishes at dinner. It has a full bar and dedicated banquet and wedding menus, so it is a common choice for family celebrations and large parties. Guests can reserve a table, order online for takeout, arrange catering, or buy frozen items to cook at home. Weekend dim sum starts at 9:30 am.

name: Fikscue Craft Barbecue
description: Fikscue serves what it calls Indo-Tex barbecue, pairing Texas-style smoked meats with Indonesian flavors. Co-owners Fik and Reka Saleh began with backyard barbecue and a pop-up selling Indonesian cookies, then opened on Park Street in November 2023. Everything on the menu is certified halal and pork-free. The menu runs from smoked brisket, beef ribs and house-made beef sausage to smoke-fried chicken and a brisket rendang plate served with rice, sambal and a spicy egg. In 2024, The New York Times named Fikscue one of the 50 best restaurants in the United States. The meats are slow-smoked, and popular items can sell out.

name: Fowl + Fare
description: Fowl + Fare, on Santa Clara Avenue, specializes in fried chicken sandwiches and fried chicken biscuits known for their crisp crust and well-seasoned spice blends. It is a small, order-focused shop. Items often sell out, so ordering ahead through its online store is encouraged, and pickup and delivery are also available. Fowl + Fare is open for lunch and dinner Wednesday through Sunday, and closes early if it sells out.

name: Genghis Khan Kitchen
description: Genghis Khan Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. According to the Downtown Alameda Business Association, its specialties include Mongolian barbecue and all-you-can-eat sushi, served alongside a budget-friendly Chinese buffet and lunch specials. The large dining room suits groups and families, and the restaurant is known for quick, friendly service.

name: Hang Ten Boiler
description: Hang Ten Boiler combines Hawaiian comfort food with the messy fun of a seafood boil. Bay Area natives Paul and Mai Wong opened it on Santa Clara Avenue in November 2006 to bring the warmth and generous portions of Hawaiian cooking to Alameda. Plate-lunch favorites such as Lava Chicken, the BBQ Mixed Plate and Northshore Garlic Shrimp share the menu with seafood combos of king crab legs, shrimp, clams and corn, along with garlic noodles and kalua pork fries. The restaurant is open 11 am to 9 pm every day and offers dine-in, pickup, delivery, catering and happy hour specials.

name: Homeskillet
description: Homeskillet is a family-owned breakfast and lunch spot on Park Street. It is known for donuts made by hand in-house, and alongside them it serves a full menu of hearty, traditional American breakfast and lunch dishes, with plates built around applewood-smoked bacon and fresh hash browns. Diners can stop in for a sit-down breakfast, pick up a box of donuts to go, or order pickup and delivery online.

name: Hong Kong City Restaurant
description: Hong Kong City is a Chinese restaurant on Park Street in downtown Alameda. It is listed in the Downtown Alameda business directory as Hong Kong City Seafood Restaurant, and seafood is the focus. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup and delivery. It sits in the heart of the Park Street business district, an easy stop for lunch or dinner downtown. Hours vary by day, so check current hours before visiting.

name: Island Taqueria
description: Island Taqueria is a casual Mexican taqueria on Park Street in downtown Alameda. The menu covers the taqueria staples: street tacos topped with onions and cilantro, regular and "super" burritos with rice, beans, pico de gallo, guacamole and cheese, loaded super nachos, and combination plates and antojitos. Tortilla chips are cut and fried in-house every day. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup and delivery, which makes it an easy choice for a quick lunch or an early dinner downtown.

name: Jim's Coffee Shop
description: Jim's Coffee Shop has been a family-run fixture in Alameda since 1960. Dimitris "Jim" Geanekos, an immigrant from Greece, opened it as a small takeout counter, and it later grew into a full-service restaurant. Today his son Tom runs the coffee shop, along with the sister location Jim's on the Course. The diner on Lincoln Avenue, just off Park Street, serves classic breakfast and lunch seven days a week from 7am to 3pm. The menu runs from omelets and eggs florentine to lunch plates such as fettuccine alfredo and salmon. Diners can eat in or order online for pickup, and large parties can reserve by phone.

name: La Penca Azul
description: La Penca Azul has served Mexican food on Park Street for more than 25 years, in the heart of Alameda's historic downtown near the Alameda Theatre. The menu covers tacos, burritos, quesadillas and enchiladas, with favorites such as carnitas, birria tacos and the oversized Super Famoso Burrito, and churros for dessert. Breakfast plates like huevos rancheros and chilaquiles are also on offer. A full bar pours signature margaritas, including peach and mango, from a selection of top-shelf tequilas. Diners can eat in, take out, order delivery or curbside pickup, or book catering. Sister locations operate elsewhere in Alameda and in Oakland.

name: Leña
description: Leña is a family-run modern Mexican restaurant on Central Avenue. Its motto is "Fire from our heritage", and the name is Spanish for firewood. Yesenia Chavez runs it with her family. Her parents come from Guanajuato, her brother-in-law leads the kitchen and her brother is sous chef. The menu offers elevated takes on traditional recipes from across Mexico, including halibut tacos, poblano enmolado, mole with Cornish game hen, oxtail and short rib birria, and whole achiote-marinated branzino. A lineup of seven signature tacos can also be ordered together. Leña serves dinner Tuesday through Sunday and brunch on weekends, and reservations are available online.

name: Mango & Mint
description: Mango & Mint is a fast-casual Vietnamese eatery on Webster Street in Alameda's West End. Owner Loan Nguyen opened it in March 2024, after running a cafe in Oakland for a decade. Guests order at the counter and build their meal from fresh ingredients on display behind the glass. The menu covers bánh mì (lemongrass pork is a favorite), vermicelli noodle bowls, rice plates, fresh spring rolls, crispy egg rolls and salads. Smoothies and Vietnamese coffee and tea round out the menu. There is limited indoor seating with a few outdoor tables, and takeout is available.

name: Moxie Steak House
description: Moxie Steak House opened on Park Street in 2024 with chef Donna Meadows in the kitchen. Meadows is a longtime Alameda food figure who managed Little House Cafe for 15 years and once owned Boniere Bakery. The dining room mixes contemporary style with a speakeasy feel: emerald-green walls, gold accents, velvet chairs, and a full bar stocked to the ceiling. The à la carte menu features filet mignon, New York strip, grass-fed ribeye and lamb chops, with seasonal sauces and a slow-cooked veal demi-glace. Sides include hasselback potatoes and chive fritters. Moxie serves dinner Wednesday through Sunday and brunch on weekends, and takes reservations online.

name: Pasta Pelican Restaurant
description: Pasta Pelican sits at the water's edge in Mariner Square, with views across the Oakland–Alameda Estuary to Jack London Square. The kitchen serves traditional Italian and American fare made with prime cuts, free-range chicken and organic produce. The menu runs from fettuccine alfredo, Bolognese and seafood ravioli to the house Pollo Pelicano and steaks such as filet mignon and New York strip. Lunch and dinner are served daily, and happy hour runs Friday through Sunday afternoons. An upstairs banquet room with waterfront views holds private events for 40 to 100 guests. Reservations are available online.

name: Peak
description: Peak is a women-owned restaurant on Webster Street that pairs two menus under one roof: brunch by day and Thai fusion by night. Mornings bring house-baked sourdough, brioche and croissants alongside pancakes, waffles, Benedicts, savory toasts and French toast. The signature dish is brioche toast with pandan cream, which draws on both halves of the menu. In the evening the kitchen turns to Thai-inspired plates built on family recipes, served with desserts and handcrafted cocktails. The dining room is cozy and decorated with art and handmade touches. Reservations and online ordering are both available. Peak is closed on Wednesdays.

name: Phnom Penh House
description: Phnom Penh House serves Cambodian cooking on Webster Street. It started in Oakland before moving to Alameda. The menu is built for sharing, with entrees that balance smoky, salty and sweet flavors. A popular choice is traop ang: grilled eggplant topped with savory ground pork, shrimp and a generous amount of garlic. The dining room is relaxed and casual, which makes it an easy choice for a walk-in lunch or a weeknight dinner.

name: Pizzeria Pappo
description: Pizzeria Pappo is chef John Thiel's casual West End follow-up to Pappo, the sit-down restaurant he ran in Alameda for many years. Thiel trained at the California Culinary Academy and cooked at Bay Wolf. Here he makes two styles of pizza: East Coast thin crust sold by the slice or whole pie, and thick, rectangular Sicilian pies. The menu also includes panini, meatballs, pastas, garlic knots, focaccia and parmigiana plates, with a few favorites like fried olives carried over from the original restaurant. Italian wines and local craft beers are on offer, and there is ice cream for dessert. It is a relaxed, family-friendly spot and handles plenty of takeout.

name: Rose's Sandwich Shop
description: Rose's Sandwich Shop is a Webster Street deli counter focused on hearty, made-to-order sandwiches. Turkey roasted in-house anchors much of the menu. It appears in the Classic with tomato and Swiss, and in the Giant, which stacks on avocado, cranberry, bacon and jack cheese. Fans of cured meats can order the Italian, layered with mortadella, ham, bologna and salami. Chicken salad, vegetarian choices and side salads round out the menu. Rose's is open daily from mid-morning into the early evening and is well suited to a quick lunch or takeout, with delivery available through the usual apps.

name: Saltbreaker
description: Saltbreaker is a neighborhood bistro at Alameda Point that serves California cooking grounded in French technique, built around seasonal produce from local farms. Chef Justin Davis's dinner menu moves from small plates such as smoked trout rillette and beef tartare to larger dishes like Ora King salmon and steak frites. A full cocktail program accompanies the food. Soon after opening, Eater SF named it one of the East Bay's hottest new restaurants. Next door, The Yard offers a more casual daytime option: a breezy patio with a full bar, oysters, chowder, fish and chips, smash burgers and a kids' menu.

name: Scolari's Good Eats
description: Scolari's Good Eats has been serving comfort food on Park Street since 2010. It was opened by Dan Nichols, who also owns The Lucky 13 bar next door, together with executive chef Mike Boyd. The menu has an East Coast accent: burgers and fries, a Taylor ham, egg and cheese on brioche, and strombolis. House-made bread, daily pizza specials, a rotating list of specials and vegan options fill out the rest. Alameda Magazine gave its burger and fries top honors in 2012, the same year the team added a vintage 1964 Airstream food truck. The truck is now available for catering, and food can also be delivered to patrons at the Lucky 13.

name: Southern Comfort Kitchen
description: Southern Comfort Kitchen brings New Orleans–style Cajun and Creole cooking to Webster Street. It is run by brothers Brett, Jason and Jeremy Brill, whose family spent 15 years as food vendors at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival. After moving to California, the family cooked at festivals, then ran food trucks, then opened restaurants in Castro Valley and Pleasant Hill before coming to Alameda in 2024. The menu covers the classics: po'boys with shrimp, catfish, oyster or soft-shell crab, jambalaya, seafood gumbo, crawfish étouffée, and blackened shrimp and grits. Service is fast-casual, with dine-in, takeout, delivery and a drive-through.

name: Southie (at Park Station)
description: Southie brings East Coast-inspired, elevated American fare to Park Station, the beer venue at 1200 Park Street in downtown Alameda. This is the second location of Southie, from restaurateur Rich Wood, who also owns Oakland's Wood Tavern and The Wolf. The kitchen keeps a seasonal menu that changes often, with sandwiches and shareable bites made to go with Park Station's drinks. Guests order the food and drinks together in a relaxed, social setting that suits a casual lunch, a game-day gathering or an evening out with friends. Online ordering is available for pickup.

name: Speisekammer
description: Since 2002, Speisekammer has served traditional German cooking on Lincoln Avenue in Alameda. Chef Peter Kahl, a native of Flensburg, Germany, runs the kitchen, where hearty classics share the menu with rotating seasonal specials, and many dishes come in regular or smaller portions. The bar pours 16 beers on tap, from German imports to local craft brews. Guests can eat in the dining room or in the outdoor beer garden, where dogs are welcome. Live music on many evenings, with no cover charge, adds to the gemütlich atmosphere.

name: Spinning Bones
description: Spinning Bones is a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand–recognized rotisserie on Park Street that blends California cooking with Japanese flavors. Owners Mike Yakura and Danny Sterling opened it in 2019. Meats such as chicken, black pepper tri-tip and pork shoulder are marinated in shio koji and roasted on spits, then served with bright sauces like chimichurri and garlic-jalapeño garum. Starters include mochiko fried chicken nuggets and cauliflower with miso butter and furikake. The room is relaxed and neighborhood-friendly, and there's outdoor seating plus beer, wine and sake to round out a meal.

name: Tahina Fresh Mediterranean
description: Tahina Fresh Mediterranean is a counter-service spot inside the Alameda Marketplace on Park Street. Rumtin Rahmani, longtime owner of The Beanery in the same marketplace, opened it with his sister Talayeh and partner Rochelle Nasab. The menu centers on herb-forward, house-made falafel in soft pita, alongside chicken shawarma, mezze plates and cilantro hummus. California touches include quinoa tabouli with avocado and saffron rice. Moroccan mint tea, pomegranate lemonade and baklava finish the meal. It's an easy choice for a quick lunch or an early dinner, and online ordering is available.

name: The Bureau 510
description: The Bureau 510 is the West Alameda outpost of an Emeryville gastropub, open on Webster Street since 2023. Owner Chalit Sangsana's menu mixes international street food with comfort classics. Burgers come with crispy fries, sometimes stacked right on top, and share the menu with banh mi, fish tacos and Korean-style short ribs. The industrial-chic space serves lunch and dinner with beer and cocktails. Happy hour runs in the late afternoon, making it an easy stop after work on the Webster Street corridor.

name: The Hobnob
description: The Hobnob is a casual, friendly neighborhood restaurant and bar in downtown Alameda, serving California comfort food made with seasonal ingredients. Dinner might start with ricotta beignets or buffalo cauliflower and move on to a Nashville spicy fried chicken sandwich, a diner burger, pan-seared salmon or a flat iron steak. Craft cocktails, beer and wine are available throughout. On weekends, brunch brings pancakes, omelets, French toast and eggs Benedict. Friday nights turn lively with karaoke, and the restaurant also offers private party space and catering.

name: Trabocco Kitchen & Cocktails
description: Trabocco Kitchen and Cocktails has brought the flavors of Abruzzo to Alameda's South Shore Center since 2013. Chef-owner Giuseppe Naccarelli grew up in the Italian region and named his restaurant after the trabocchi, the wooden fishing huts along its Adriatic coast, echoed by a net installation above the dining room. The menu leans toward coastal cooking, including salt cod, octopus and brodetto alla vastese seafood stew, alongside handmade pasta with rabbit ragù, oxtail ravioli and rotisserie rabbit. A full cocktail program makes it a good fit for anything from lunch to a celebratory dinner.

name: Waki
description: Waki is a Japanese restaurant on Webster Street in West Alameda focused on sushi and carefully prepared Japanese dishes. The menu runs from bluefin tuna tataki and hamachi carpaccio to signature rolls such as the dragon roll, along with cooked favorites like beef and salmon teriyaki. For a broader sampling, there's the "Waki's Tasting" option. Wine and beer are served. Waki is open for dinner nightly and for lunch on Sundays, and it also offers takeout ordering, catering and private parties for larger groups.

name: Wild Ginger
description: Wild Ginger serves Chinese street food on Park Street in downtown Alameda, with a menu built around noodles. Wide, chewy biang biang hand-pulled noodles and cumin lamb noodles sit alongside hearty beef noodle soup, cold noodles and malatang. Other favorites include rou jia mo, a lamb "burger" on griddled bread, spicy tingly beef, and sour and spicy pork dumplings. The kitchen emphasizes fresh ingredients and carefully balanced seasoning. There's indoor and outdoor seating, and it's open for lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday, with online ordering for takeout.

name: 310 Eatery - LA Style Street Food
neighborhood: Albany (San Pablo Ave near Solano Ave)
description: 310 Eatery brings the flavors of Los Angeles street and comfort food to San Pablo Avenue in Albany. Owner Aaron Fong got his start in restaurants as a server at Grazzy Burgers, the burger spot that once occupied this same address, and he launched 310 Eatery in Walnut Creek in 2014 before reopening it here in 2018. The menu centers on burgers and beer, with playful LA-inspired creations such as the 405 Traffic Jam Burger, bacon jam fries, and a Little Tokyo Po' Boy built on soft-shell crab with unagi aioli. It is a casual stop for dine-in, takeout, or delivery.

name: 900 Grayson
hours: Mon-Fri 8-10:45am (breakfast), 11:30am-2pm (lunch); Sat 8am-2pm; Sun closed (per Visit Berkeley; verify)
description: Tucked into a pink-fronted corner building at Grayson and Seventh streets, 900 Grayson is a longtime West Berkeley favorite for breakfast and lunch. The kitchen puts creative spins on American comfort food, drawing on quality, seasonal ingredients and the occasional Asian accent. It has long been known for the Demon Lover, a plate of spicy fried chicken over buttermilk waffles, along with a natural-beef burger topped with applewood-smoked bacon and house barbecue sauce. The low-key, neighborly room fills quickly on weekdays and Saturday mornings, and outdoor seating and takeout are also available.

name: Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen
description: Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen is Downtown Berkeley's slice of New Orleans, set on Shattuck Avenue at Kittredge Street near the downtown theaters and BART. Founder Robert Volberg opened it to share Southern hospitality and Louisiana flavors with the Bay Area, and the menu leans on Big Easy classics: jambalaya, gumbo, buttermilk fried chicken, Creole barbecue shrimp, and beignets for dessert, with Abita beer to wash it down. The casual, kid-friendly dining room comes with New Orleans music, and there is outdoor seating in warmer months. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available.

name: Anja's
hours: Tue-Sat 8:30am-3pm (as reported at 2024 opening; verify)
description: Anja's is a small German cafe from chef Anja Voth, who ran the beloved Gaumenkitzel on San Pablo Avenue for 13 years before closing it in 2024. Working with her husband, Kai Flache, she reopened on University Avenue that summer with a lighter, daytime menu she describes as California cooking with German love, built on organic and sustainable ingredients from her longtime suppliers. Expect creamy oat porridge, savory potato-egg muffins, soups, and German sheet cakes such as poppyseed and apple, plus Gugelhopf. Guests can linger on the patio beside rose gardens or grab something to go.

name: Ashby Eatery
hours: Wed-Thu & Sun 8am-4pm; Fri-Sat 8am-7pm; Mon-Tue closed (per Toast ordering page)
description: Ashby Eatery is a relaxed neighborhood cafe on Adeline Street, directly across from the Ashby BART station, that opened in fall 2025 in the former Flacos space. It serves elevated breakfast and lunch all day, from biscuit egg sandwiches, the Berkeley Scramble, and banana bread French toast to a spicy honey fried chicken sandwich, a vegan BLTA, grain bowls, and kale Caesar salad. Smoothies, coffee, beer, and wine round out the drinks, and there is a kids' menu plus happy-hour tacos and snacks. Covered and open-air seating make it an easy stop, and dogs are welcome.

name: Bangalore Blues (by Pochys)
neighborhood: Upper Solano Ave / Thousand Oaks (at The Alameda)
hours: Tue-Sun 11am-3pm and 4-9pm (Hoodline, Apr 2026); pochys.com says closed Thursdays - verify
description: Bangalore Blues is the sit-down evolution of Pochys, restaurateur Aravind Pochiraju's South Indian spot on Solano Avenue, reborn in early 2026 with a dining room awash in deep blue down to the plates. The kitchen draws on Bangalore street food and home cooking, roasting whole spices in-house and making its own ghee. Look for crisp masala and ghee dosas, soft idli, Chicken 65, gobi Manchurian, kathi rolls, and donne biryani made with seeraga samba rice. For a deeper dive, an $80 multi-course Karnataka tasting menu features dishes such as koli saaru and chicken chops.

name: Bangkok by the Bay
neighborhood: West Berkeley (Aquatic Park area, near Berkeley Bowl West)
hours: Mon-Fri lunch 11:30am-2:30pm, happy hour 5-6pm, dinner 5-8:30pm; Sat happy hour 4:30-5:30pm, dinner 4:30-9pm (per official site)
description: Bangkok by the Bay is a family-run Thai restaurant that opened in November 2024 in West Berkeley's Aquatic Park district, in the tree-lined courtyard space long home to Riva Cucina. Co-owners Sung Makawatsakul, who leads the kitchen, and Nantika Julakasilp serve familiar favorites alongside dishes less often seen on Bay Area menus. Standouts include laab gai presented in a purple cabbage leaf, a massaman curry of slow-cooked bone-in short ribs, and carefully garnished pad Thai. The bright dining room and large outdoor patio suit weekday lunches, happy hour, dinner, and private events.
tags: Laab gai in purple cabbage leaf

name: Brezo
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 10:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-8pm; Fri 10:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-9pm; Sat 8:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-9pm; Sun 8:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-8:30pm (per official site)
description: Brezo is a chef-owned California-Mexican restaurant on lower Solano Avenue in Albany, run by co-chefs Heather Mervine and Hector Hernandez. After starting in Point Richmond in 2017, the pair moved in early 2024 to the former Rendez-Vous Cafe Bistro space, where Mervine had begun her executive chef career, bringing her story full circle. The kitchen makes its own non-GMO masa, bakes pastries in-house, and cooks with seasonal California produce. Favorites include chilaquiles verdes, blueberry pancakes with blueberry butter, gorditas, braised lamb, and the Brezo Burger, served for brunch, lunch, and dinner indoors or on a sunny patio.

name: Califa's Greens (styled "Califas Greens" on its website)
hours: Sun 10am-3:30pm; Mon-Tue 10am-7:30pm; Wed 10am-3:30pm; Thu-Sat 10am-8:30pm (per website; Visit Berkeley lists slightly different hours)
description: Califa's Greens is a family-run scratch kitchen on University Avenue. Owners Zeiri Guzman, Annia Guzman and Margarito Gallardo worked at La Capilla, the restaurant that used to occupy the space, and took it over in early 2021. The menu mixes fresh, vegan-friendly bowls and salads with Mexican and Latin American comfort food: kale and beet bowls, cochinita pibil and carnitas tacos, chilaquiles, huevos rancheros and enchiladas, all served with housemade salsas. Fresh-squeezed juices and smoothies go well with the lighter plates, and churros, alfajores and tres leches cake round things out. It's a relaxed, welcoming stop for breakfast, lunch or an early dinner.

name: Chez Mansour Restaurant & Wine Bar
hours: Daily 11:30am-9:30pm (per official website; OpenTable shows a weekday afternoon break, 2:30-4:30pm)
description: Chez Mansour is a Lebanese and Mediterranean restaurant and wine bar on Solano Avenue in Albany, with an old-fashioned, candlelit dining room made for lingering. The kitchen makes its mezza in house, including hummus, baba ghannouge, falafel and grape leaves, which work well shared over a glass of wine. There are also grilled kababs of lamb, beef, chicken and seafood, shawarma, lamb chops, and baked eggplant with pomegranate sauce, with baklava to finish. Some evenings bring live music, including jazz duos and occasional belly dancing. Tables outside on Solano are a nice option on warm days.

name: Chez Panisse
hours: Restaurant: Mon-Sat, two dinner seatings. Café: lunch Tue-Sat, dinner Mon-Sat. Closed Sunday.
description: Chez Panisse is Alice Waters' landmark North Berkeley restaurant and one of the places most closely tied to Californian cuisine and the farm-to-table movement. The kitchen cooks from peak-season produce and local sources, and the menus change every day. Downstairs, the main dining room serves a four-course set dinner in two nightly seatings, with the open kitchen and wood-burning oven in full view at the back. Upstairs, the more casual café offers an à la carte menu at lunch and dinner. It's a place food lovers seek out on purpose, and reservations open a month ahead.

name: DH Noodles and Grill
neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
hours: Mon-Fri 11:30am-3:30pm & 4:30-8:45pm; Sat-Sun 11:30am-8:45pm (per Chowbus)
description: DH Noodles and Grill opened on Telegraph Avenue in spring 2026 and serves the regional cooking of Northwestern China. The focus is Lanzhou-style hand-pulled noodles, served in rich soups, tossed dry or stir-fried. The menu also has heartier dishes such as da pan ji, a big plate of chicken stew, and cumin-spiced lamb, plus Northwest-style grilled skewers, cold appetizers, and fried rice and pilaf. A few blocks from campus, it's a casual spot for a filling bowl of noodles at lunch or dinner, and it also does takeout and delivery.

name: Divan — Modern Turkish Cuisine
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm, Sat-Sun 11am-2:30pm; dinner daily 5-8:45pm (per website)
description: Divan is a modern Turkish restaurant on Fourth Street that opened in June 2026, run by the team behind San Francisco's Taksim. The name refers to the central seating area of a traditional Turkish home, and the idea is hospitality: plates meant for sharing and taking your time over. The menu includes mezze such as hummus and muhammara, pide flatbreads, kebabs, cabbage rolls and grilled branzino, plus a generous Turkish breakfast for two with menemen and çılbır. The bright space has wood and tile details, a full bar with craft cocktails and sangria, and a covered patio.

name: Dolly's
description: Dolly's is a family-owned Italian restaurant and wine bar on San Pablo Avenue in El Cerrito, run by owner Dolly Batathota. Its signature dish is fettuccine finished tableside in a 100-pound wheel of Parmigiano-Reggiano, an idea Batathota brought home from a trip to Florence. It's served plain or topped with smoked salmon or prosciutto, and it's become the restaurant's best-known draw. The rest of the menu covers Italian classics, with a selection of wines to go with them. Dolly's also caters weddings, birthdays and corporate events, and offers takeout and delivery.

name: Duo Grill House
hours: Daily 8am-3pm (per website)
description: Duo Grill House is a neighborhood breakfast and lunch spot on Solano Avenue in Albany, serving hearty morning plates every day until mid-afternoon. Benedicts are a specialty, with five versions ranging from the classic to smoked salmon and a hash-topped take. There are also omelettes and scrambles (including one named for Albany), steak and eggs, Belgian waffles, and fried chicken and waffles. For something with more kick, there's a smothered breakfast burrito, chilaquiles and huevos rancheros. Egg plates come with Parmesan roasted potatoes or hash browns, and the counter now serves espresso. Dine in, take out or order delivery.

name: El Mono | Fresh Flavors of Peru
description: El Mono brings the bright, homestyle flavors of Peru to San Pablo Avenue in El Cerrito. Owners Matt Khadivian and Daniela Diaz built a lively, colorful dining room decorated with art inspired by the Nazca Lines. The rotisserie chicken is the signature, and the menu covers Peruvian classics such as lomo saltado and ají de gallina, a creamy chicken stew made with ají amarillo. Fried green plantains with chimichurri and yuca with rocoto aioli are popular starters. Guests can dine in, reserve for larger parties, or order takeout, and the restaurant also caters group events. A second El Mono has since opened on Fourth Street in Berkeley.

name: FAVA
hours: Tue–Sat 11am–3pm; closed Sun–Mon
description: FAVA is a small, daytime lunch counter on Vine Street in North Berkeley. It is run by chefs Sylvie Osborne Calierno and Jeremy Scheiblauer, who met while cooking at Chez Panisse. Sylvie had earlier opened her own restaurant in Spain, and Jeremy led the kitchen at a San Francisco restaurant before returning to Chez Panisse. The pair took over the space long occupied by the Juice Bar Collective. Their cooking is fresh, simple and built around seasonal ingredients, and service is casual and counter-style. The relaxed setting makes FAVA an easy choice for a neighborhood lunch, and families with children are welcome.

name: Gather
hours: Mon–Fri 11am–2pm & 4–8:30pm; Sat–Sun 10am–2pm & 4–8:30pm
description: Gather opened in 2009 on the ground floor of the David Brower Center, steps from the UC Berkeley campus. It was founded by Eric Fenster and Ari Derfel of Back to Earth Catering and has become a showcase for organic, sustainably sourced California cooking. The seasonal menu draws on dozens of local farms and ranches and is designed for omnivores, vegetarians and vegans alike. Standouts include a vegan pizza made with cashew cream and a seasonal roast chicken, served with cocktails made from sustainable spirits. The dining room is built largely from reclaimed materials, including seat cushions stitched from old leather belts. Gather serves lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, and hosts private events.

name: Gusto
hours: Mon–Thu 11am–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–10pm; Sun 11am–9pm
description: Gusto opened on Shattuck Avenue in January 2026 as Berkeley's first Algerian fast-food spot. Owner Abdullah Bouhafs runs it with the aim of sharing the everyday street food of his home country with a new generation. Merguez, the spiced North African sausage, is the star and comes in lamb, beef or chicken. The menu also includes Algerian-style wraps and tacos, shawarma and burgers. Traditional sweets such as maqrout, ghribiya and kunafa are made fresh daily. Everything is halal, prices are modest, and videos and photos of Algerian landscapes set the mood. Gusto offers dine-in, takeout and delivery.

name: Homeroom Berkeley (Homeroom Mac+Cheese)
hours: Daily 11am–midnight
description: Homeroom began in Oakland in 2011 as a restaurant devoted almost entirely to macaroni and cheese. Its Berkeley outpost brings that playful concept to West Berkeley's Gilman District, in a warehouse building shared with other local food businesses. The menu offers creative takes on the comfort classic. The most popular is a Gilroy garlic mac, and there are also truffle and Buffalo chicken versions, among many others. The Berkeley location keeps late hours and is set up for pickup, delivery and catering, which makes it an easy choice for a group meal or a late-night craving.

name: In the Wood
hours: Sun–Thu 11:30am–8:30pm; Fri–Sat 11:30am–9pm
description: In the Wood calls itself a gastropub for the Elmwood neighborhood: a casual, contemporary place for neighbors to meet over food and drinks on College Avenue. It has been open since 2018. The kitchen is built around a wood-fired oven that turns out pizzas alongside small and large plates made with local meats, fish and produce, with vegan and gluten-free options available. The bar focuses on locally brewed craft beers and sustainable wines, and happy hours are a regular feature. In the Wood serves lunch, dinner and brunch, with indoor and patio seating as well as takeout.
tags: local craft beer and sustainable wines

name: Inn Kensington
neighborhood: Kensington (Arlington Ave business district, just north of Berkeley)
hours: 7:30am–2:30pm; closed Tuesdays (per aggregator; verify)
description: Inn Kensington is a small neighborhood cafe on Arlington Avenue in Kensington, in the hills just north of Berkeley. Locals come here for a classic American breakfast and lunch. The menu leans on hearty morning favorites: homemade biscuits, corned beef hash, omelettes and scrambles, pancakes and waffles, and a chorizo breakfast for those who want some spice. The atmosphere is relaxed and family-friendly, with a cozy dining room and some outdoor seating. Guests can eat in or order takeout, and seasonal specials keep regulars coming back.

name: Juanita & Maude
hours: Tue–Sat 5–9pm
description: Juanita & Maude is an intimate, chef-driven restaurant on San Pablo Avenue in Albany. Chef Scott Eastman, formerly chef de cuisine at Berkeley's Corso, opened it in 2017 with co-owner Ariane Owens. It is named for his grandmother Juanita and his mother Maude. The kitchen offers Eastman's personal take on American cooking: a daily-changing, ingredient-driven menu of refined comfort food that draws on influences from around the world. Diners can sit in the lively dining room, anchored by a zinc bar, or on a heated back patio. A full bar with creative cocktails, wine and beer rounds out the dinner-only experience.

name: KAOKAO Grill
hours: Tue-Sun 11:30am-3pm, 4pm-8:30pm; closed Mon (per aggregator listing)
description: KAOKAO Grill is an owner-run spot on College Avenue in the Elmwood that brings American-style smoked barbecue together with Asian flavors and noodle bowls. Diners come for glossy char siu pork served over rice and for hearty bowls of noodles topped with smoky brisket, balanced by cool sides like spiced eggplant salad and tangy cucumbers, with house sodas to drink. The casual, loft-like room has seating on two levels, and the kitchen also handles takeout and delivery for those who want to bring their barbecue home. It is an easygoing neighborhood choice for lunch or an early dinner.

name: Kiraku
hours: Tue-Thu 5:30pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5:30pm-11pm
description: Kiraku, whose name means "to relax," has brought the spirit of a Japanese izakaya to Telegraph Avenue since 2011. Chef Daiki Saito, who trained in French cooking in Japan before working in Bay Area sushi and yakitori kitchens, runs it with his wife, Sanae. Evenings begin with a warm towel and move through small plates and grilled skewers meant for sharing over drinks. Saito is a certified sake sommelier, and the list of sake and shochu runs deep, with a bottle-keep program for regulars and Asahi draft poured Japanese-style. Many of the stoneware dishes are made by the chef himself.

name: Korean Superette
hours: Sun-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm
description: Korean Superette on Solano Avenue is part neighborhood market, part casual Korean eatery. It opened in 2022 in the longtime home of the restaurant Rivoli. Shelves and deli cases around the dining room hold house-made banchan, kimchi (including vegan versions), noodles and pantry staples for cooking Korean food at home. From the kitchen come comforting plates such as rice bowls with soup, tteokbokki and rotating specials like gochujang-braised pork ribs. Guests can eat inside or on the outdoor seating, or pick up ready-made meals to go. The shop also offers catering, private event space and a meal subscription.

name: La Marcha Tapas Bar
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; brunch Sat-Sun 10am-3pm; dinner daily 4pm-10pm; happy hour Mon-Fri 4pm-6pm; late night Fri-Sat 10pm-12am
description: La Marcha Tapas Bar brings a lively Spanish spirit to San Pablo Avenue. Owner Sergio Emilio Monleón learned the rules of Valencian paella from his Spanish grandmother, and the pans that come out of the kitchen show it: classic paella mixta with prawns, chicken and chorizo, and the all-pork "tres cerditos." A long list of tapas fills out the table, from sizzling head-on garlic shrimp to salt cod croquetas with romesco and tortilla española. The MICHELIN Guide recommends it. There is an L-shaped bar with weekday happy hour, weekend brunch and late nights on Fridays and Saturdays, and groups are welcome.

name: La Note Restaurant Provençal
hours: Mon-Fri 8am-2pm; Sat-Sun 8am-3pm
description: La Note has been serving Provençal-style breakfast and lunch on Shattuck Avenue since 1997, and it has become one of Downtown Berkeley's best-loved morning spots. The kitchen is known for its pancakes, especially lemon gingerbread and oatmeal-raspberry, as well as pain perdu and omelets like the Côte Ouest filled with ratatouille. The dining room has the relaxed charm of a country bistro, and a quiet courtyard patio out back is a favorite on sunny days. Weekend lines are common, and the restaurant takes reservations through its website.

name: Lao Garden Restaurant & Bar
hours: Mon-Sat 11am-3pm, 5pm-9pm; Sun 12pm-3pm, 5pm-9pm (as of April 2025)
description: Lao Garden is chef Kanlaya Palivan's showcase for Laotian cooking on San Pablo Avenue. She briefly ran Rose Garden Uptown in Oakland while waiting on Berkeley permits, then opened here in January 2025. The menu leans into Lao classics such as nam khao (crispy rice salad wrapped in lettuce), laab gai, funky green papaya salad and kua mee Lao, alongside familiar noodles like drunken noodles. The room is bright and cheerful, with orange chairs, colorful lanterns and a wall of flowers and butterflies. There is a bar, and the restaurant serves both lunch and dinner.
tags: thum lao lao green papaya salad

name: Larb Thai Food & Tapas
hours: Lunch 11:30am-2:10pm, dinner 5pm-8:10pm (per DoorDash); closed Tuesdays (per Tripadvisor)
description: Larb Thai Food & Tapas takes its name from larb, the zesty minced-meat salad of northeastern Thailand's Isaan region, and that dish anchors the menu here. This small, unpretentious restaurant in a San Pablo Avenue strip mall in El Cerrito has a warm, family-run feel. Beyond larb made with meat or prawns, regulars order the crispy rice ball salad, pork hock, khao soi and well-made noodle staples like drunken noodles and pad see ew. Spice levels run from mild to true Thai heat, and the kitchen will work around dietary needs. It serves lunch and dinner for dine-in and takeout.

name: Li's Knife Cut Noodle
description: Li's Knife Cut Noodle is a family-run noodle house that opened on Center Street in December 2025, following its first location in San Mateo. Owner Jian Han's parents spent more than two decades making noodles in China, and their method drives the menu: dough is shaved by hand straight into boiling water, giving wide, tender, chewy strands. Bowls come in a range of homestyle preparations, with dumplings on the side, and the house offers free noodle refills for anyone still hungry. The Downtown Berkeley dining room is roomier than the original, with more than 20 tables.

name: Phosho Dough (Phởsho Dough)
hours: About 11am-6:40pm per DoorDash (verify)
description: Phosho Dough is a Vietnamese restaurant on San Pablo Avenue in West Berkeley. It is the second location of an Oakland eatery that started on Telegraph Avenue, and it is owned by Richard Kha. The menu is built on comforting noodle soups, including lemongrass beef pho and hu tieu ga, a shredded-chicken noodle soup. Grilled pork and shrimp vermicelli bowls, crispy cha gio egg rolls and banh mi sandwiches round it out. Portions are generous and the setting is casual, so it works well for a quick lunch or an early dinner, whether eating in or taking out.
tags: hu tieu ga chicken noodle soup

name: Lulu's Little Kitchen
hours: Wed-Sun 11:30am-7:30pm; closed Mon-Tue (brunch items Sat-Sun)
description: Lulu's Little Kitchen is chef Mona Leena's casual, counter-service take on the California-meets-Palestinian cooking she first served at her full-service restaurant Lulu. In early 2026 Leena reworked the Solano Avenue space into a more affordable, everyday format built around halal rice bowls, roti wraps, salads, sides and coffee, with fillings such as braised lamb, chicken kebab and falafel alongside hummus and toum fries. The bright, sunny room suits a relaxed lunch or an early dinner, and takeout is available. On weekends, brunch brings back some of Lulu's best-loved dishes, including knafeh pancakes, baklava French toast and shukaquiles.

name: Mercado 925
hours: Per OpenTable: Sun-Mon, Tue, Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm (Wednesday not listed; verify)
description: Mercado 925 is a colorful Mexican restaurant and bar on University Avenue in West Berkeley, opened in 2023 by restaurateur Juan Romo, who is also behind Casa Latina and La Mission. The kitchen puts an inventive spin on regional dishes such as mole poblano tacos, enmoladas de Puebla, chiles rellenos, Baja fish tacos and Sonora-style ceviche. The bar is known for its deep list of mezcal and tequila. In 2025 the restaurant added m925, an annex with high ceilings, rattan furniture, a semi-private mezzanine and a bottle shop. There is also an upstairs terrace. Mexican brunch and weekday happy hour make it an easy fit for dates, families and small celebrations.
tags: Modern Mexican; mezcal and tequila bar

name: Mezzo
neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
hours: Daily 8am-9pm (closes 6:30pm Tuesdays); breakfast 8-11am
description: Mezzo carries on the legacy of Cafe Intermezzo, a Telegraph Avenue favorite that opened in 1983 and was lost to a fire in 2011. The cafe reopened as Mezzo in 2017, keeping the original recipes while pairing a modern look with vintage pieces saved from the old cafe. It is best known for very large salads, including the popular Chef Salad with house poppyseed dressing, as well as made-to-order sandwiches on house-made honey wheat bread and daily soups. Breakfast is served in the morning. A ramp connects Mezzo to Raleigh's Pub next door, so guests can have their sandwich with a local craft beer.

name: Mount Everest Restaurant
neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
hours: Per Visit Berkeley: Mon-Tue and Thu-Sun 11am-9:15pm; closed Wednesday
description: Mount Everest Restaurant is a family-run Nepali and Indian restaurant on upper Telegraph Avenue, a few blocks south of the UC Berkeley campus. It opened in 2010 and is now run by the second generation of the family. It has become a regular stop for students and neighbors looking for Himalayan comfort food made with traditional recipes and fresh ingredients. The menu covers both Nepali and North Indian dishes, including steamed momo dumplings, samosas, chaat, biryani, dishes from the tandoor and a wide range of curries. The dining room is relaxed and welcoming, and the restaurant also offers takeout.

name: Noodle Dynasty
neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
hours: Tue-Sun 12-4pm and 5-8pm (per restaurant site); closed Monday
description: Noodle Dynasty is a small, busy Chinese noodle shop on Telegraph Avenue near the UC Berkeley campus. It specializes in hand-pulled noodles served in rich, slow-cooked broths. The house special beef rib noodle soup, made with a bone-in rib, is the dish most people come for. Lamb shank noodles, spicy pickled cabbage with fish, and stir-fried dishes round out the menu. Guests order on tablets, the open kitchen works quickly, and the compact dining room is usually full and noisy. At peak times a line often forms down the sidewalk, drawing students and East Bay noodle fans alike.
tags: House special beef rib noodle soup

name: O2 Eatery
hours: Daily 8am-3pm (per East Bay Express at opening; verify)
description: O2 Eatery is a bright breakfast and brunch spot on Solano Avenue. It opened in August 2024 in the former Delirama deli space, run by the previous owners of Sumo Sushi on San Pablo Avenue. The dated deli was fully remodeled into a calm, green-toned dining room with a closed kitchen. The menu centers on eggs, with omelets, scrambles, benedicts and breakfast sandwiches on brioche, along with a goddess breakfast bowl and croffles. A popular side is crispy potatoes finished with chimichurri. It serves breakfast and lunch only, making it a good choice for a weekend brunch or a relaxed weekday meal.

name: Peace Natural Vegan Food
hours: Daily 11am-2:30pm and 4:30-8pm (per Tripadvisor listing; verify)
description: Peace Natural Vegan Food is a small plant-based restaurant on Solano Avenue run by chef-owners Palden and Gyatso. It serves wholesome, organic vegan meals from a menu that changes every day with the season. Instead of a long à la carte list, diners choose a set plate. The Modest and Generous meals include soup, grains, legumes, greens, mixed vegetables and salad, while the Trio pairs soup with three dishes of the day. Momos and fresh rolls are available as starters, and the house-made desserts contain no refined sugar. Teas, kombucha, and organic vegan beer and wine complete the menu.

name: Picnic (Picnic Rotisserie)
neighborhood: San Pablo Ave at Solano Ave, Albany
description: Picnic is a neighborhood rotisserie and charcuterie shop at San Pablo and Solano avenues in Albany. It was founded by two neighbors, butcher-chef Susannah Schnick and chef and business lead Leslie Nishiyama. Schnick learned charcuterie at Fatted Calf and whole-animal butchery at Cafe Rouge and Clove & Hoof. The pair began by selling at local farmers markets before opening their storefront. Picnic is built around takeout, with golden rotisserie chickens, sausages, salami, pâté, porchetta and chicken liver mousse, plus salads, sides, pickles, sandwiches and a weekly-changing menu. Much of the food is made in-house from locally sourced meat.

name: Roses on Adeline Bar & Kitchen
hours: Mon-Wed 4pm-10pm; Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-midnight; Sun 4pm-10pm (happy hour daily 4-6pm)
description: Roses on Adeline is a neighborhood bar and kitchen on South Berkeley's Adeline Corridor, built around the idea of food as a way to connect people. The evening-only menu leans seasonal and Californian, with bar favorites like a smashburger next to lighter plates such as crudo, tuna tartare, ceviche, tostadas and pasta. Drinks cover wine, beer and cocktails, and the wine list has a soft spot for chilled reds and skin-contact bottles. Guests can sit at the bar or in banquettes, and the dining room opens onto an attached garden that brings in daylight and fresh air. Walk-ins are welcome, reservations are available, and happy hour runs daily.

name: Sakana Sushi & Roll
hours: Mon-Sat 11:45am-2:15pm and 4:30pm-8:15pm; Sun 3:30pm-8:15pm (per online ordering site)
description: Sakana Sushi & Roll is a small neighborhood sushi spot on Arlington Avenue in Kensington, just over the hill from North Berkeley. The menu covers the classics, including nigiri, sashimi, chirashi and assorted moriawase platters, alongside donburi and poke bowls. Its playful side shows in the long list of special and baked rolls, such as the Lion King, which is crab and avocado under baked salmon, and a rice-free house special wrapped in pickled radish around salmon, tuna, unagi, mango and avocado. Vegetarian rolls round out the options. Guests can eat in the cozy dining room or order takeout, including party platters for sharing.

name: Sam's Log Cabin
neighborhood: Albany (San Pablo Avenue, on the Berkeley border)
description: Sam's Log Cabin is a longtime breakfast and brunch destination housed in a genuine log cabin on San Pablo Avenue in Albany. The building dates to 1930, when it was ordered as a kit from a Sears catalog, and it has reportedly served as a speakeasy and a bookies' hangout along the way. Today the kitchen, run by co-owner and chef Rhasaan Fernandez with partner Mike Daillak, turns out hearty morning plates with Southern and Californian touches: chilaquiles with house-made chips, braised collard greens with poached eggs and cornbread, seasonal pancake specials and a fried chicken sandwich. Seating is outdoors on the patio, and the vibe is relaxed, homey and dog-friendly.

name: Tanzie's
neighborhood: Southwest Berkeley (Dwight Way near San Pablo Ave)
hours: Mon and Thu 10am-2pm; Fri-Sun 8:30am-2pm; closed Tue-Wed (per website)
description: Tanzie's is a chef-owned Berkeley cafe that gives brunch a Northern Thai accent. Chef Krissana "Tanz" Tussanaprasit, a Kin Khao alum who also ran a restaurant in Chiang Mai, opened it in early 2024 with partner Jezreel "Jae" Rojas, a veteran of Kin Khao and La Cocina. Many recipes come from Tanz's family. Standouts include pa tong go, Thai-style beignets with sweetened condensed milk; "lava eggs," soft scrambled eggs over rice with savory toppings such as nam prik ong; Thai spiced sausage; and a jasmine Thai tea chia bowl, plus matcha drinks. The small, cottage-like space has cozy nooks, plenty of plants and a fireplace. Reservations are taken through Tock.
tags: lava eggs with nam prik ong

name: TAROCCO
hours: Mon-Fri 11am-2:30pm; weekends reserved for private events
description: Tarocco is a sunny weekday lunch cafe on Ninth Street in West Berkeley, modeled on the relaxed counter bars of Barcelona. It began in 2020 as a pandemic meal-delivery service and opened a physical location in 2022. Owner Sequoia Del Hoyo, co-founder of Sequoia Diner, runs it with chef Jason Botterill, who previously cooked at Chez Panisse and London's River Cafe. Guests choose from a counter of composed seasonal salads and ready-made Mediterranean dishes built on produce from local farms, then eat in the bright, rustic dining room or take their food to go. Tarocco also offers catering, weekend private events and Club Tarocco, a weekly meal subscription.

name: The Hidden Café
neighborhood: West Berkeley (Addison St at Strawberry Creek Park)
hours: Tue-Sun 8:30am-5pm; closed Mon (per joe coffee listing)
description: The Hidden Café is a small, bohemian-feeling daytime cafe tucked into a building beside Strawberry Creek Park in West Berkeley, which makes finding it part of the appeal. It is a relaxed place to linger over coffee or tea, with indoor tables and outdoor seating in a leafy, park-like setting. The drinks menu goes beyond espresso to include turmeric lattes, chai and matcha, while the kitchen offers pastries and treats such as a sweet potato brownie, along with a rotating weekend brunch. The cafe also has ties to local artists and musicians, adding a creative, community-minded feel to this neighborhood hideaway.

name: Tipsy Yeti Restaurant & Bar
description: Tipsy Yeti Restaurant & Bar brings a lively, modern take on Nepali cooking to San Pablo Avenue. Owners Sujan Shrestha and Rubin Sainju opened it in 2025 in a longtime restaurant space, pairing the flavors of Kathmandu with a Californian, comfort-food streak. Momo lead the menu, filled with paneer, chicken, lamb or bison and also served in jhol broth, alongside choila (spiced duck with beaten rice), goat curry and chili chicken. Crossover dishes like a bison burger, Himalayan pizza and tornado fries fill out the list. A full bar pours signature cocktails, wine and mocktails, and live music on weekends keeps the family-friendly dining room busy.

name: Via del Corso
hours: Sun and Tue-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm; closed Mon (per website)
description: Via del Corso is a North Berkeley Italian trattoria on Shattuck Avenue, in the space long home to the beloved Tuscan spot Corso. When Corso closed during the pandemic, Berkeley-born restaurateur Peter Chastain revived it under a new name borrowed from a grand boulevard in Rome. The kitchen draws on central Italy and other regions, and it brought back some of Corso's best-loved dishes, including bistecca alla Fiorentina and pollo al burro, chicken in a rich butter sauce. The team's opening lineup included veterans of Walnut Creek's Prima. It is a relaxed, dinner-only place for wine, pasta and long meals with family and friends, and it takes reservations.

name: ACRE Kitchen and Bar
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11:30am-2pm; Midday daily 2-5pm; Dinner Sun-Thu 5-8:30pm, Fri-Sat 5-9pm; Happy hour daily 4-6pm (per official site, Sept 2026)
description: ACRE Kitchen and Bar fills the two-level space inside Rockridge Market Hall that was long home to Oliveto. Chef-owner Dirk Tolsma and managing partner Pete Sittnick opened it in late 2022 with a menu of Californian and Mediterranean cooking touched by North African and Middle Eastern flavors. Downstairs, a relaxed bar and cafe serves an all-day menu; upstairs, a brighter dining room filled with art looks out over College Avenue. Regulars come for the honey-glazed rotisserie chicken, a brisket burger on a house-baked bun, whole roasted branzino and seasonal plates built on Northern California produce. Weekday lunch, weekend brunch, a daily happy hour and dinner service make it an easy stop at almost any hour.

name: Almond and Oak
hours: Tue-Fri 5-9pm dinner; Sat brunch 10am-2pm and dinner 5-9pm; Sun brunch 10am-2pm; closed Mon (per official site)
description: Almond and Oak is a neighborhood restaurant on Grand Avenue run by chef Rico Rivera, an Oakland native who graduated from Skyline High School, trained at the Culinary Institute of America in Hyde Park, and learned farm-driven cooking at the Lark Creek Inn. He opened the restaurant in December 2018 around scratch cooking and locally sourced ingredients. The seasonal New American menu might include a grilled New York strip with creamy greens, steak tartare, fried sweet corn polenta or roasted kabocha squash with figs and hazelnuts. Weekend brunch brings beignets and cornbread to the table. A full bar, indoor and outdoor seating, reservations and private events round out a place that feels rooted in the city its chef grew up in.

name: Aloha Club
hours: Tue-Wed 3-10pm; Thu 3pm-midnight; Fri 3pm-2am; Sat noon-2am; Sun noon-10pm; closed Mon (per official site)
description: Aloha Club is a family-run Fruitvale bar that describes itself as roughly a century old, making it one of the neighborhood's longest-running watering holes. It keeps an old-school feel, with a jukebox, a pool table and games on the screens, but it also mixes scratch cocktails alongside craft, import and domestic beers and a broad spirits shelf that leans into tequila and mezcal. A garden patio out back is a draw on warm evenings. Food comes from partners: In Nena's Kitchen serves Cambodian beef noodle soup, rice plates and egg rolls, and the La Grana taco truck turns out quesabirria, fish tacos and aguachile. Weekday happy hour runs until 7pm, and the space hosts birthdays, viewing parties and fundraisers.

name: Aman Cafe
hours: Mon-Fri 10:30am-3:30pm; Sat-Sun 9:30am-3pm (per official site)
description: Aman Cafe is a daytime cafe on Broadway built around Malaysian roti canai, the flaky, buttery flatbread served with curries and dipping sauces. Owner Tiyo Shibabaw opened it in 2021 after running Teni East, a Burmese restaurant next door, from 2016. She came up through the Burma Superstar group, and her cooking brings together Southeast Asian technique, her Ethiopian heritage and a California sensibility. Alongside roti plates filled with curried chicken or vegetables, the menu offers rice bowls such as ginger chili chicken and tofu-potato, garlic noodles with tofu, smoothies and house drinks like ginger-turmeric lemonade. The cafe serves breakfast and lunch every day, offers takeout and online ordering, and caters events.

name: Bardo Lounge & Supper Club
hours: Mon-Thu 5-10pm; Fri-Sat 5-11pm; closed Sun (per Michelin Guide); official site says Monday through Saturday
description: Bardo Lounge & Supper Club brings a 1960s supper-club spirit to Lakeshore Avenue, in the space once home to Michel Bistro. Owners Seth and Jenni Bregman opened it in 2018 with a lounge of cozy alcoves and a more traditional upstairs dining room, all dressed in throwback style. The kitchen revisits retro dishes such as porcupine meatballs and broccolini casserole with modern touches, and a Dinner Party Menu lets the kitchen choose for the table. Cocktails are central, from house-made tinctures and cream soda to shareable punch bowls, with several non-alcoholic options. Bardo appears in the Michelin Guide and is a longtime date-night favorite. Every seat, including at the bar, is by reservation.

name: Battambang
hours: Mon-Sat 11am-8pm; closed Sun (per official site)
description: Battambang has served Cambodian home cooking in Oakland's Chinatown since 1993, and it is one of the few places in the Bay Area devoted to the cuisine. Named for Cambodia's second-largest city, the modest, unfussy dining room puts its attention on the food. Longtime favorites include amok trei, catfish curry steamed in banana leaf; sach chrouk aing, grilled lemongrass pork with a lime and fish sauce dip; prahok ktiss, a minced pork dip served with fresh vegetables; tamarind-sauced Battambang noodles; and sour lemongrass soup. Smoked eggplant, crab fried rice and papaya salad also appear on the menu, with a jackfruit and coconut custard for dessert. Lunch and dinner run Monday through Saturday, with takeout and delivery.

name: Bellanico Restaurant and Wine Bar
hours: Brunch Fri-Sun 10:30am-2:30pm; Dinner Wed, Thu, Sun 5-8:30pm and Fri-Sat 5-9pm; Ombra Hour Wed-Sun 5-6pm (per official site)
description: Bellanico Restaurant and Wine Bar is a Glenview neighborhood spot from chef-owner Chris Shepherd, who first opened Aperto in San Francisco's Potrero Hill. The name blends his daughters' nicknames, Bella and Nico. The kitchen cooks rustic Italian food with seasonal California ingredients and makes its own cured meats, fresh pasta and bread every day. Dinner can mean house pastas, grilled meats or a prix fixe menu, and brunch runs Friday through Sunday. The wine list, overseen by wine director Elizabeth Frumusa, leans toward Old World and Italian bottles, with more than 20 wines by the glass and bottles for retail sale. Ombra Hour, the house take on Italian happy hour, fills the early evening Wednesday through Sunday.

name: Belotti Bottega
description: Belotti Bottega is the casual Piedmont Avenue pasta shop from chef Michele Belotti, the Bergamo-born cook behind Belotti Ristorante e Bottega in Rockridge. It opened in 2017 in the former Gregoire space as a simpler way to bring his fresh pasta into the neighborhood. The counter sells fresh, frozen and prepared pastas to eat in or take home, along with ready-made sauces, bread, cookies and imported Italian pantry goods such as olive oil and salt. It suits a quick bowl of pasta at lunch or a stop for dinner supplies on the way home, and pickup and delivery ordering are available online.

name: Belotti Ristorante E Bottega
hours: Mon-Sat 11am-10pm; closed Sun (per Michelin Guide)
description: Belotti Ristorante e Bottega is a small, welcoming Italian restaurant on College Avenue run by chef Michele Belotti and Joyce Belotti. Born and raised in Albino, near Bergamo, Michele trained in Michelin-starred kitchens in Lombardy and Piemonte, moved to California in 2011 and cooked at San Francisco's Ristobar before opening his own place in Rockridge around 2016. The menu focuses on simple, traditional Piemontese cooking and house-made pasta, such as heirloom-grain spaghettini with tomato and burrata, brasato over polenta with a nebbiolo reduction, and tortino, a spinach flan with egg yolk and truffle. The bar draws a loyal crowd of regulars. The restaurant is listed in the Michelin Guide and takes reservations through Resy.

name: Bird & Buffalo
hours: Tue-Sun lunch 11:30am-2pm, dinner 5-10pm; closed Mon (per official site)
description: Bird & Buffalo serves what its founder calls Thai soul food: the simple, rustic dishes that farm families in the Thai countryside cook for themselves. Todd Sirimongkolvit, also behind Soi 4 in Rockridge and Basil Canteen in San Francisco, opened it on Telegraph Avenue in January 2018 in the former Rosamunde Sausage Grill space. The name recalls the birds that ride on water buffalo in rice paddies. Bright plastic tablecloths and an easygoing pace echo a roadside eatery, while the menu leans toward the Northeast, with grilled meats, green papaya somtum in Thai or Lao style, larb, street-stand curries, khao soi noodles and mango sticky rice. It serves lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday and is listed in the Michelin Guide.

name: Bistro 4293
hours: Tue-Sun 11:30am-2:30pm and 5-9pm; closed Mon (per official site)
description: Bistro 4293 brings Azerbaijani and wider Caucasus cooking to Piedmont Avenue, a cuisine shaped by Persian, Central Asian and Middle Eastern traditions. Owner Anar Usubov grew up in Khojaly, Azerbaijan, left his hometown during the 1992 conflict and came to the United States in 2015. After years of searching for the flavors he grew up with, he decided to cook them himself, and the restaurant is the result. The menu features classics such as khan plov, a celebratory rice dish, lyulya kebab of seasoned ground meat, and dolma, grape leaves stuffed with meat. Named for its street address, the bistro serves lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday and offers reservations through OpenTable.

name: Bombera
hours: Mon and Wed-Sat 5-9pm; closed Tue and Sun (per Michelin Guide)
description: Bombera occupies a former fire station in the Dimond District, and its name, Spanish for firewoman, nods to both the building and the wood fire at the center of its kitchen. Chef-owner Dominica Rice-Cisneros ran Cosecha in Swan's Market for a decade before opening Bombera in April 2021. Her cooking pairs a locavore, fine-dining background with respect for generations-old Mexican technique. Ash from the wood-fired oven is used to nixtamalize corn for house-made masa and tortillas, and dishes such as duck leg confit with nutty mole verde, black beans and blue corn tortillas show the approach. Bombera holds a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide, and the San Francisco Chronicle has named it the Bay Area's best Mexican restaurant.
tags: duck leg confit with mole verde

name: Brotzeit Lokal
hours: Mon-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri 11am-9:30pm; Sat 10:30am-9:30pm; Sun 10:30am-9pm (per official site)
description: Brotzeit Lokal is a German beer garden on the Oakland Estuary, opened in 2013 by Krista Bailey, a former college professor, and Tony Granieri, an architectural designer. The pair wanted a family-friendly place to gather outdoors, and they converted a former seafood restaurant into a waterfront biergarten with picnic tables overlooking the water and a guest dock. The kitchen makes its own sausages, including smoked frankfurters, and serves them with fresh pretzels, wiener schnitzel and seasonal specials, along with a strong list of German beers. Weekend brunch, a happy hour, a deli menu and a dog-friendly patio keep it busy, and seasonal celebrations such as Oktoberfest carry the spirit of gemutlichkeit, or community and togetherness.

name: Burma Superstar
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm; dinner Mon-Thu 5-9:30pm, Fri 5-10pm; Sat 11:30am-10pm; Sun 11:30am-9:30pm (per OpenTable)
description: Burma Superstar brings the flavors of Myanmar to Temescal, where it has been a Telegraph Avenue fixture for well over a decade. The restaurant family began in San Francisco's Richmond District in 1992 under founder Desmond Tan and later grew to Oakland and Alameda. The Oakland dining room is lively and open, with long booths suited to groups. The menu draws on Burma's neighbors in India, China and Thailand. The fermented tea leaf salad is the best-known dish, and platha, samosa soup, coconut curries, noodles and a good range of vegetarian and vegan options fill out the menu. It serves lunch on weekdays and dinner nightly, and takeout is available.

name: Cambodian Street Food
hours: Mon & Wed-Sat 11am-7pm; Sun 11am-5pm; closed Tue (per Restaurantji aggregator; verify)
description: Cambodian Street Food is a small family-run kitchen on Foothill Boulevard at 21st Avenue that cooks Khmer dishes to order. The setup is casual and mostly takeout. People come from all over Oakland for its low prices and home-style cooking. Regulars order the grilled beef and chicken skewers over rice, salt-and-pepper dry-fried pork ribs with garlic and jalapeño, and banh xeo, the turmeric-yellow crepe served with fresh herbs and house fish sauce. Lemongrass-heavy kreung stir-fries and soups, larb and egg rolls round out the menu. Every dish is cooked fresh, so a wait is normal, and calling ahead helps.

name: Cholita Linda
hours: Daily 11am-10pm (per official site)
description: Cholita Linda is run by Vanessa Chavez, who grew up in Oakland, and her husband Murat Sozeri. It started as a stand at the Jack London Square farmers market in 2008 and opened its Temescal restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in 2014. The cooking is eclectic Latin, shaped by Chavez's Peruvian grandmother and her travels. The fried fish tacos made it famous, and they sit alongside carne asada, carnitas and spit-roasted chicken tacos on handmade tortillas, a Cubano sandwich and fresh aguas frescas. The space is bright, with tropical plants and music, and there is a hidden courtyard out back. It is open daily for dine-in, online ordering and catering.

name: Crogan's Montclair
hours: Mon-Sat 11:30am-9pm; Sun 11:30am-8pm (per official site)
description: Crogan's Montclair is a long-running neighborhood pub and restaurant in the middle of Montclair Village. Families, sports fans and groups of friends all end up in its roomy dining room and bar. The menu is classic American pub food made with fresh ingredients. Fish and chips is the signature dish, and braised short ribs, crab sandwiches, buffalo wings and blackened ahi also appear. A full bar pours traditional and modern cocktails, and big-screen TVs show the games. Crogan's serves lunch and dinner daily. It hosts birthday parties, rehearsal dinners and corporate events, and takeout and delivery are available through several ordering platforms.

name: Dan Sung Sa Restaurant
hours: Open late, until about 1-2am (verify; sources conflict)
description: Dan Sung Sa is a well-loved Korean soju bang (drinking pub) on Telegraph Avenue near Uptown, and it keeps going long after most Oakland kitchens have closed. The room is dark and energetic, covered in vintage movie posters, and it was named after an old Seoul cinema. It works well for big groups sharing plates over soju and beer. The menu is Korean bar food: crispy fried Cornish game hen with salt-and-pepper dipping sauce, galbi, wings, kimchi fried rice and the famously over-the-top loaded fries topped with Korean barbecued pork. It is a sister spot to nearby Kang Tong Degi and a local favorite for late-night eating.

name: Daughter Thai Kitchen
