hours: Mon-Thu 11:30am-2pm & 5-8:30pm; Fri 11:30am-2pm & 5-9pm; Sat 12-3pm & 5-9pm; Sun 12-3pm & 5-8:30pm (per official site / Visit Oakland)
description: Daughter Thai Kitchen specializes in southern Thai cooking, which is richer, spicier and more seafood-focused than Bangkok-style fare, and serves it on Medau Place in Montclair Village. It opened around the start of 2017 from Kasem "Pop" Saengsawang and Ling Chatterjee, the team behind San Francisco's Farmhouse Kitchen, with partner Kimberly Gamble, whose mother runs Lanna Thai in Livermore. The dining room is warm and homey, with wooden tables, golden temple bells and a family bookshelf. Hat Yai fried chicken, kang kua prawns served in a coconut, and crispy rice salad are among the standouts. It serves lunch and dinner daily and offers reservations, takeout and catering.

name: Daytrip
hours: Closes 8pm (per SF Standard, June 2025); full schedule not verified
description: Daytrip Counter is the relaxed second act of Daytrip, the Temescal restaurant from husband-and-wife owners Finn Stern and Stella Dennig. The original opened in 2021 and became known for fermented, vegetable-driven cooking and natural wine. Bon Appetit named it one of the country's best new restaurants of 2022, and Stern was a 2024 James Beard semifinalist. The owners closed that format at the end of 2024 and reopened the same space in spring 2025 as a counter-service spot built around rotisserie chicken. Whole brined-and-roasted birds come with bright salads, sides like gigante beans with pesto and Caesar fries, and plenty of dipping sauces. The disco ball is still there.

name: Degrees Plato Tap Room
description: Degrees Plato is a family-friendly tap room, bottle shop and kitchen on MacArthur Boulevard in the Laurel District. Husband-and-wife owners Richard and Mercedes opened it in May 2017. Richard used to sell beer, and he built the business around one rule: pour only beer from independent brewers. The rotating tap list is joined by seven cooler doors of bottles and cans to drink there or take home, plus wine and cider. The kitchen makes Oakland-style tacos, tortas and snacks from scratch with local and Mexican ingredients. The owners want it to be a neighborhood gathering place, somewhere neighbors can meet over a beer and a plate of tacos.

name: FOB Kitchen
hours: Weekends are brunch only (per Michelin); full hours not verified
description: FOB Kitchen serves modern Filipino home cooking in Temescal. Chef Janice Dulce and her wife Brandi started it as a San Francisco pop-up in 2015 and opened the Telegraph Avenue restaurant in late 2018. The small room has whimsical wallpaper and an easygoing island feel, and there is a bar to wait at with a cocktail. The menu is built on family-style Filipino classics: pork adobo, thrice-cooked lechon kawali, sweet-sour sinigang, beef mechado and Janice's slow-roasted ribs glazed with coffee, coconut beer and banana ketchup. Turon and suman are the desserts. The Michelin Guide recognizes it with a Bib Gourmand, and weekends are devoted to brunch.

name: Gangnam Jajang
hours: Mon-Thu 11am-3pm & 5-9pm; Fri 11am-11:30pm (with afternoon break); Sat 11am-11:30pm; Sun 11am-9pm (per Wanderlog aggregator; verify)
description: Gangnam Jajang is a Korean-Chinese noodle house in the Koryo Village plaza on Telegraph Avenue. It took over the space once held by Koryo Jajang. The noodles are made in-house, and the kitchen says key sauce ingredients arrive from South Korea every week. The namesake jajangmyeon comes in a glossy, savory black bean sauce with pork and vegetables, and jjamppong is its fiery seafood noodle soup. The fried dishes get the most attention, especially kkanpunggi, the crisp fried chicken in a garlicky, spicy sauce, and a honey butter chicken. Rice bowls, fried rice, tteokbokki and dumplings round out the menu. The room is modern, and takeout and delivery are available.

name: Ghost Town Brewing - Laurel Biergarten & Kitchen
description: Ghost Town Brewing's Laurel Biergarten & Kitchen is the second home of the West Oakland brewery known for its heavy-metal, death-themed branding and bold beers. Co-founder Ryan Nosek and team took over the former 4505 Burgers & BBQ space on MacArthur Boulevard in 2021. They turned it into a roomy beer garden with an in-house kitchen and a long tap wall of Ghost Town brews, along with wine and cider. All the beer is still brewed at the original Adeline Street brewery. The Laurel location has become a neighborhood hangout for growlers, food and long afternoons outdoors. Berkeleyside and Oaklandside readers named it the East Bay's best beer garden and taproom in late 2025.

name: Grand Lake Kitchen
hours: Daily 9am-9pm; brunch until 3pm; weekday happy hour 3-6pm; dinner from 5pm (per official site)
description: Grand Lake Kitchen is an all-day cafe and full bar on Grand Avenue near Lake Merritt, owned by May Seto Wasem and her husband Dave. It started as a small deli with a counter and a few tables and grew into one of the neighborhood's go-to brunch spots, then expanded to the Dimond District and San Francisco's Noe Valley. May Wasem describes the food as comfort and classics. Brunch runs until 3pm with dishes like chilaquiles and eggs Benedict. Later come the porchetta sandwich with broccoli rabe pesto, Reuben fries, fried green tomatoes, matzoh ball soup and a burger. It offers weekday happy hour, a dog-friendly patio, reservations and catering.

name: Grand Lake Kitchen - Dimond
hours: Closed Mon; Tue-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sun 9am-9pm; brunch to 3pm; weekday happy hour 3-6pm (per official site)
description: Grand Lake Kitchen's Dimond District location is the bigger sibling of the Lake Merritt original. It is a spacious all-day cafe and full bar on MacArthur Boulevard run by owners May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem. It opened about five years after the Grand Avenue flagship and has close to 6,000 square feet of dining room and patio. The menu is the same comfort-and-classics style: brunch favorites until 3pm, then sandwiches, salads, soups, burgers and shareable plates like Reuben fries and fried green tomatoes at dinner. It offers weekday happy hour and a dog-friendly patio, and takes reservations for brunch and dinner. It is closed Mondays.

name: Gum Kuo
description: Gum Kuo is a long-running, no-frills Cantonese restaurant on 9th Street in the heart of Oakland's Chinatown. It has been a neighborhood fixture for well over a decade and is best known for comforting everyday staples rather than banquet fare. Bowls of silky rice porridge, some topped with fish, minced beef or abalone, land on nearly every table, alongside wonton noodle soup, beef brisket noodles and steamed rice noodle rolls. A window of roast duck, char siu and roast chicken supplies plates to eat in or boxes to take home, and clay pot dishes round out the menu. Expect a casual, bustling room and quick, straightforward service.

name: Huangcheng Noodle House
hours: Wed-Mon 10am-9pm; closed Tuesday (per official site)
description: Huangcheng Noodle House is Jimmy Huang's counter inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland, where the draw is hand-shaved noodles in the style of Shanxi province. Huang, a third-generation noodle maker who earlier had a career as a professional acrobat in China, slices ribbons of dough straight into boiling water, giving them chewy, ruffled edges that hold sauce well. The menu covers noodle soups, dry and stir-fried noodles, fried rice, appetizers and vegetarian options, with spicy Chongqing-style street noodles a popular order. It is a casual food-hall setting with communal seating, and in 2024 Huang opened Huang Cheng Potsticker, a handmade dumpling stall just down the hall.

name: InNenasKitchen
hours: Weekends only (exact hours not confirmed; check Instagram)
description: InNenasKitchen is Oakland native Nena Neak's Cambodian noodle operation, now running as a weekend counter-service residency at the Aloha Club on Fruitvale Avenue. Neak started it in March 2024 as a home kitchen, selling bowls of kathiew, the Cambodian beef noodle soup, from her Fruitvale residence. Its rich broth, built from beef ribs, neck bones, fish sauce and toasted aromatics like star anise, ginger and onion, drew such crowds that she had to move out, first to a warehouse and then, in 2026, to the Aloha Club. The family-run crew also serves shrimp rolls and pig-ear sausage, and bowls often sell out, so arriving early is wise.

name: Italian Colors Restaurant
description: Italian Colors is a family-owned Californian-Italian restaurant that has served the Montclair district in the Oakland hills since 1993. Founder and chef Alan Carlson trained at the Culinary Institute of America and cooked at Auberge Bertone in New York and Scott's Seafood in Oakland before opening it. His approach is that good food should be fun and approachable, and the menu pairs Italian staples and fresh pasta with Mediterranean influences and nightly seasonal specials. An extensive wine list backs up the kitchen, and after three decades it remains a neighborhood dinner spot in the hills. It also takes part in Oakland Restaurant Week. Reservations are taken by phone.

name: Itsumo
description: Itsumo is a Japanese bistro that opened in summer 2026 on MacArthur Boulevard in Oakland's Laurel District. It took over a space that previously housed another Japanese restaurant, Pa's Papa, and continues the storefront's role as a casual neighborhood spot for Japanese comfort food. The menu covers bento boxes, sushi and specialty rolls, and bowls of ramen, suited to a quick lunch, a relaxed dinner or takeout. Delivery is also offered through third-party apps. As one of the Laurel's newest restaurants, it is still building its reputation, so check its Instagram for current hours and menu updates.

name: Jo's Modern Thai
hours: Wed-Sun 12pm-9pm; closed Mon-Tue (per Michelin Guide)
description: Jo's Modern Thai is a Laurel District restaurant from Oakland native Kao Saelee, named for his wife, Jo. Since opening in 2021, it has drawn attention for Thai cooking that keeps the cuisine's bold balance of sweet, sour, salty and spicy while freely adding new ideas. Signature plates include drunken noodles with smoky barbecued brisket and a pork burger seasoned like laab with fresh herbs, and the blue sticky rice with mango sorbet is a popular dessert. The Michelin Guide gives it a Bib Gourmand for good cooking at a fair price. The dining room is lively and casual, open for lunch and dinner, and takes reservations through OpenTable.
tags: blue sticky rice with mango sorbet

name: Joodooboo
hours: Tue-Sat 12pm-3pm and 4:30pm-8pm; closed Sun-Mon (per official site and Michelin)
description: Joodooboo is chef Steve Joo's small Korean banchan shop and restaurant on Market Street in North Oakland, built around fresh tofu, or dooboo, made in-house. Joo, who trained at Chez Panisse and learned tofu-making during an apprenticeship in Korea, makes it from domestic organic soybeans, using seawater as the traditional coagulant. The tofu comes fresh or lightly fried with a savory sauce, alongside rice bowls, chilled acorn noodles, rotating soups and a changing lineup of vegetable banchan, pickles and kimchi from local farms. Food & Wine named Joo a Best New Chef in 2025, and the Michelin Guide awards a Bib Gourmand. Tofu and banchan are also sold to take home and at Bay Area farmers markets.

name: Kakui Sushi
hours: Tue-Sun lunch 11:30am-2pm, dinner 5pm-9pm (to 9:30pm weekends); closed Monday (per official site)
description: Kakui Sushi is a neighborhood Japanese restaurant on Mountain Boulevard in Montclair, a regular stop for local sushi fans at both lunch and dinner. The open layout lets diners watch the chefs at work as they prepare nigiri of salmon, tuna and white fish along with a long list of specialty rolls, including the Dragon, Alicia and Spicy Scallop rolls. Cooked starters such as Dynamite Shrimp balance the raw selections. Kakui suits a casual meal in the dining room and also offers takeout and delivery, with online ordering, a rewards program and gift cards. Reservations can be made through OpenTable.

name: Kotobuki Japanese Restaurant
hours: Mon-Thu 4pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 11:30am-2pm and 4:30pm-9pm; Sun 4:30pm-9pm (per official site)
description: Kotobuki is a family-run Japanese restaurant in Montclair Village that has served the neighborhood since 1990 and is now managed by Jun Liang and his family. Generations of local customers have come for its combination dinners, customizable bento-style meals that are the menu's best seller. Fresh sashimi and specialty rolls such as the Rainbow Roll share the menu with teriyaki, ramen and Japanese curry, so it works for sushi lovers and cooked-food fans alike. Diners can sit at the sushi counter or in the dining room, and the restaurant offers online ordering, takeout and delivery. Lunch is served on Fridays and Saturdays, and dinner nightly.

name: Lucky Three Seven
hours: Tue-Sun 11am-9pm; closed Monday (per Oaklandside, Aug 2023; confirm current)
description: Lucky Three Seven is a family-run Filipino kitchen on upper Fruitvale Avenue, opened in May 2013 by cousins Mark Legaspi and Artgel 'Jun' Anabo with their Auntie Cielito, after years of running a catering business in Oakland. Its storefront, painted in the red, blue and gold of the Philippine flag, turns out generous plates of home-style comfort food. The G-Fire wings, based on a family grandmother's recipe, are the signature, alongside sizzling short ribs with garlic rice, oversized lumpia, adobo and silog breakfast plates. The restaurant is also known for community work such as block parties and food drives. Orders are for dine-in or pickup, and payment is cash, Venmo or Zelle only.

name: MAMA Oakland
hours: Dinner from 5pm (Resy); full weekly schedule not confirmed
description: MAMA is a warm, retro-styled Italian-American restaurant on Grand Avenue near Lake Merritt, opened in 2019 by husband-and-wife team Stevie Stacionis and Josiah Baldivino, the founders of Oakland's Bay Grape wine shop. It honors Stacionis's grandmother, Maria Germano Stacionis, and the idea of a Sunday supper at an Italian grandmother's table. Dinner is a three-course, prix-fixe red-sauce menu built around pastas such as spaghetti with sugo, linguine with pesto and mushroom risotto, with add-ons like meatballs in sugo. Baldivino, an advanced sommelier, created the wine program, which uses playful icons to make choosing a glass easy. Caramel banquettes, pink accents and plants set a cozy, slightly campy mood.

name: Mi Grullense
hours: Mon-Thu 9am-10pm; Fri 9am-10:30pm; Sat 8am-10:30pm; Sun 8am-10pm (per NetWaiter; Visit Oakland lists slightly different hours; confirm)
description: Mi Grullense Restaurant & Tequila Bar is a sit-down Mexican restaurant on Fruitvale Avenue in the heart of Oakland's Fruitvale district, a neighborhood long known for its Mexican food and culture. It is open from breakfast through late evening every day, serving Mexican plates from its kitchen alongside a full bar focused on tequila. The restaurant sometimes hosts live entertainment, which makes it a lively place for a night out as well as a family meal. Takeout, delivery and catering are available, and seating is first-come, first-served. It recently introduced a new menu.

name: Montclair Egg Shop
hours: Weekdays 8am-2pm; weekends 8am-3pm (per official site)
description: Montclair Egg Shop has served breakfast and lunch in Montclair Village since 1974. It was part of a string of seven egg shops that restaurateur Ed Baker opened across Oakland and Berkeley, starting in downtown Oakland in 1963. After more than five decades it remains a neighborhood gathering place, now owned by Miguel Barron. The menu covers classic egg breakfasts and a rotating list of specials, from polenta dishes to crab cake Benedict, plus Mexican-inspired plates like breakfast tacos and chilaquiles. Sandwiches, crepes and salads fill out the lunch side. It is open seven days a week for breakfast and lunch.

name: Moo Bong Ri
hours: Phone (510) 654-4606. Hours in 2020 press: Mon-Fri 10:30am-2:30pm & 4-10pm; Sat-Sun 10:30am-10pm (verify; may be outdated)
description: Tucked into the back of Koryo Plaza on Telegraph Avenue, Moo Bong Ri is a Temescal go-to for hearty Korean soups, stews and casseroles. The Oakland outpost of a Korea-born restaurant brand, it has been serving the neighborhood since around 2017. The menu leans into comfort cooking: bubbling gamjatang pork-bone stew, beefy galbi tang, spicy yukgaejang, soondae guk and generous platters of bossam and braised galbi jjim, all served with banchan. Portions are built for sharing, the room is cozy and unfussy, and it is the kind of place to go for a restorative bowl on a cool Bay Area evening. Takeout and phone orders are also available.

name: Mr Liu Noodle House
hours: Official site: 10:30am-7:30pm, closed Thursday. Yelp/Apple Maps show 10:30am-8pm (conflict; verify)
description: Mr Liu Noodle House brings the fiery, numbing flavors of Chongqing to a small storefront on 11th Street in Oakland Chinatown. Opened in 2024, the shop specializes in Chongqing xiao mian, the chili-oil-slicked wheat noodles that are a street-food staple in southwest China, and the kitchen makes its noodles and dumplings by hand. Beyond the signature spicy noodles, the menu covers Sichuan cold noodles, zhajiang noodles, several beef noodle soups and a lineup of rice noodles served bubbling in clay pots, from tomato meatball to braised spare ribs. It is a casual, quick-service spot well suited to a solo lunch, with online ordering and delivery available.

name: Mugunghwa Korean Restaurant (Oakland)
hours: Lunch and dinner (specific hours not verified)
description: Mugunghwa is a home-style Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in Temescal, the second location of a well-loved El Cerrito original. It opened in summer 2025 in the former Hancook space, run by the same owners, and quickly drew a following for home-style cooking. The menu spans comforting soups and stews, braised galbijjim short ribs, crisp Korean fried chicken, bibimbap bowls, chilled mul naengmyeon noodles and barbecue dishes. It is open for lunch and dinner, a menu that works for sharing several dishes or for a quick weekday meal, and takeout and delivery are available.

name: NIDO's BackYard
hours: Opens Mon at 12pm (Mon-Tue 12-9pm per Yelp); late happy hour 8-10pm has been promoted on Instagram (verify current)
description: NIDO's BackYard is a festive Mexican restaurant and margarita garden at the edge of Jack London Square. Husband-and-wife team Silvia Hernández-McCollow and Cory McCollow opened it in 2019 as a tribute to Nido, the restaurant they launched in the neighborhood in 2012. The largely open-air space centers on seasonal Mexican cooking paired with a deep list of agave spirits, mezcal and margaritas, and its motto, 'Mi BackYard es su BackYard,' sums up the laid-back, communal mood. The patio is dog-friendly, it runs happy hour specials, and it is easy to reach by ferry or BART. The same family also runs Odin Mezcalería nearby on Oak Street.

name: Oakland Street Food Co.
hours: Not verified
description: Oakland Street Food Co. is a casual counter-service spot on 13th Street in Downtown Oakland that mixes the flavors of the city's street-food scene. Its menu leans on Baja-style and birria tacos alongside garlic noodles and grilled chicken, a mashup that draws on Mexican and Filipino influences. Portions are hearty and the format is built for speed, making it a convenient stop for downtown workers, BART riders and anyone grabbing lunch between errands. Online ordering for pickup is available directly through the restaurant, and the shop also serves drinks and small bites.

name: Ohgane Oakland
hours: Daily 11am-10pm
description: Ohgane has grilled Korean barbecue on the corner of Broadway and 39th Street since 2005, and this Oakland dining room is where the local mini-chain began. Guests cook at built-in tabletop grills, and the signature galbi short rib is hand-cut, scored and marinated for days in a soy, pear and garlic blend before it reaches the table. Alongside the barbecue come bulgogi, spicy pork, bibimbap, hot stews and a spread of banchan made fresh each morning. The lively room, with ventilation hoods over every grill, suits groups as well as a weeknight dinner, and it serves lunch and dinner every day, with reservations available.

name: Parche
hours: Mon 5-9pm; Tue-Thu 11:30am-2pm & 4-9pm; Fri-Sat 11:30am-10pm; Sun 11:30am-9pm. Happy hour Tue-Thu 4-6pm, Fri-Sun 3-5pm (bar and lounge only)
description: Parche is a contemporary Colombian restaurant on Broadway in Uptown Oakland, founded by chef Paul Iglesias, a Bay Area restaurateur with deep Colombian roots. Since opening in January 2023, it has reworked traditional Colombian cooking with California ingredients, and its name, a Colombian word that evokes getting together with friends, sets the tone for a lively room built around shared plates. The kitchen is entirely gluten-free, and the restaurant serves lunch, dinner and a happy hour at the bar and lounge, with reservations available. It is recognized in the MICHELIN Guide and has hosted cultural events such as food-and-music pairing menus during Hispanic Heritage Month.

name: Pizzaiolo
hours: Dinner from 5pm (Yelp shows Mon-Tue 5-9pm; full current schedule not verified)
description: Pizzaiolo has been a Temescal fixture on Telegraph Avenue since 2005, serving wood-fired pizza and pasta shaped by Northern California's farm-driven cooking. The restaurant describes its food as organic and local, with a menu that changes constantly as the seasons turn. Pizzas come out of the wood-burning oven, and pastas and other Italian-inspired plates change with whatever local farms are harvesting. The restaurant bills itself as a love letter to Northern California, and its founder trained at Chez Panisse, the Berkeley restaurant that shaped the region's ingredient-first style. After two decades on the avenue, it remains a neighborhood gathering spot for an unhurried dinner, and reservations help on busy nights.

name: Pomet
hours: Wed-Sun 5-9pm; closed Mon-Tue
description: Pomet is a farm-rooted Californian restaurant on Piedmont Avenue from Aomboon Deasy, the farmer behind K&J Orchards, a longtime fixture at Bay Area farmers markets known for its stone fruit, pears and other orchard crops. Since opening in 2022, it has served as a direct line from farm to table: fruit and produce come from the family orchard and other local growers, meats come from regenerative ranchers, and pruned orchard wood fuels the wood-fired oven. The seasonal menu might pair oysters with Asian pear mignonette or fill pasta with mushroom puree and finish it with celery root miso butter, and meals often end with a gift of fresh fruit. Pomet is listed in the MICHELIN Guide and takes reservations for dinner Wednesday through Sunday.

name: Prescott Market West Oakland
hours: At opening (Apr 2025): Mon-Sat 8am-9pm (Almanac to 10pm Fri-Sat); Sun 8am-8pm. Vendor hours vary; verify current
description: Prescott Market is a food hall and community gathering place on 18th Street in West Oakland that opened in spring 2025. It brings several East Bay vendors under one roof: Pizzeria Violetta, an Almanac Beer taproom, Woo Can Cook, Fast Times Burgers, Highwire Coffee, Cafe Noir and a butcher-deli counter, among others. A large back patio and plenty of outdoor seating make it an easy place to linger with kids or friends. Beyond everyday dining, the market hosts a seasonal monthly night market with live music, local makers and street food, plus weekly Sunday markets, and it is available for private events.

name: Puerto Rican Street Cuisine
hours: TEMPORARILY CLOSED (fire damage, Sept 2026); Yelp lists a scheduled reopening of Sept 30, 2026
description: Temporarily closed. Puerto Rican Street Cuisine is the East Oakland comeback restaurant of chef Eric Rivera, one of the Bay Area's best-known champions of Boricua cooking and co-founder of the beloved Borinquen Soul. Opened on 23rd Avenue in the San Antonio neighborhood in 2025, it revives many of his signature dishes: slow-roasted pernil, chicken encebollado, carne guisada, arroz con gandules, empanadas, pasteles, alcapurrias and sweet and savory plantains. It also serves favorites from his Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives days, such as loaded plantain canoas and fried-chicken mofongo. The restaurant began as a takeout operation, offers catering and has hosted hands-on pilón painting experiences. It is temporarily closed after a September 2026 fire; check before visiting.

name: Qi Wei House
hours: Not verified
description: Qi Wei House is a casual Downtown Oakland counter on 15th Street specializing in Hawaiian-style barbecue and Asian fusion rice bowls. The menu centers on teriyaki plates and bowls made with chicken, beef, salmon or shrimp, alongside kalbi short ribs and mixed barbecue combos served over rice. Seafood lovers can also find a loaded bowl of salmon, unagi and tuna with crab salad, edamame and crisp vegetables, finished with teriyaki and a house special sauce. Built for quick lunches and takeout, it also offers party packs for office gatherings and group orders, plus delivery through the major apps.

name: Rose Garden Uptown
hours: Mon-Fri lunch from 11am (partial listing seen; full hours not verified)
description: Rose Garden Uptown serves Lao and Thai cooking from a bright, modern dining room at San Pablo Avenue and 19th Street, near the Oakland Ice Center. It opened in 2024 with a mission of cooking from family recipes with fresh ingredients, bringing more Lao cooking to Uptown. The menu offers several styles of laab, Lao beef jerky, sai oua herb sausage, fresh Lao spring rolls and mok pa, catfish steamed in banana leaf with herbs, alongside Thai favorites such as curry with roti. Table service is available, many guests order to go, and the restaurant also handles catering and events.

name: Saffron Kitchen, Restaurant & Bar
hours: Sun-Thu 12pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-10pm (per official website)
description: Saffron Kitchen brings the flavors of Afghanistan and its Silk Road neighbors to College Avenue in Rockridge. Founder Akbar Arghandiwal, an Afghan American entrepreneur who spent two decades building businesses abroad before settling in the Bay Area, opened the restaurant in 2023 with chef Abdul Yawari leading the kitchen. The menu leans on Afghan home cooking with Persian and Mediterranean touches: qabuli pallaw with lamb shank, kobideh kabobs, lamb-filled steamed dumplings, and crispy eggplant with yogurt, alongside generous vegetarian platters. A full bar pours house cocktails and mango lassi, and a daily happy hour draws neighborhood regulars. Reservations, takeout, catering, and private events are all available.

name: Saucy Oakland
hours: Conflicting: Yelp snippet lists Mon closed, Tue-Wed 11:45am-2pm lunch; Facebook lists dinner Wed-Sat from 5:30pm. Confirm with restaurant.
description: Saucy Oakland is the creative project of locals Tony Ngo and Jenni Nguyen, who launched it in 2015 as a pop-up built around roughly twenty homemade sauces. Chef Ngo, trained in Japanese and French cooking, draws on Japanese and Thai flavors, and the kitchen still makes its marinades and sauces in-house. After time on Telegraph Avenue, Saucy settled in 2022 into a storefront on 8th Street at the edge of Old Oakland and Chinatown. The menu mixes playful small plates such as hamachi shooters and Thai corn dogs with Basque cheesecake, and the restaurant has offered a multi-course chef's tasting with sake pairings. Reservations are taken through OpenTable, and catering is available.

name: Seoul Gom Tang
hours: Conflicting third-party listings: Wanderlog shows daily 11am-3pm and 5-10pm; TripAdvisor shows longer hours. Confirm with restaurant.
description: Seoul Gom Tang is a modest, family-run Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue devoted to slow-simmered beef soups. Its namesake gomtang arrives milky and unseasoned, so diners add sea salt, black pepper, and radish kimchi at the table, and it comes in versions with brisket, beef knuckle, or a mixed bowl with tripe and tendon. Oxtail soup, galbitang, cold mul naengmyeon, spicy pork-bone and potato stew, seafood pancakes, and dumplings round out the menu, served with fresh banchan. The setting is casual, with table service and takeout, and it is a comforting stop for anyone craving a restorative bowl of Korean broth.

name: Sequoia Diner
hours: Mon 9am-2pm; Wed-Sun 8am-2pm; closed Tue (per Nosh, Dec 2025; may have changed after sale)
description: Sequoia Diner has been a Laurel District fixture on MacArthur Boulevard since 2015, when Andrew Vennari and Sequoia Del Hoyo set out to make diner classics with top-quality ingredients. The kitchen is known for fluffy biscuits, buttery pastries, and pecan sticky buns, along with seasonal specials like a red flannel hash of beets and yams topped with poached eggs. A coffee bar and booths make it an easy neighborhood gathering spot, and weekend waits are common. Sequoia won the 2025 Nosh Award for best breakfast in the East Bay and was named to the San Francisco Chronicle's Top 100 list in 2025. New owners took over in early 2026 and pledged to keep what regulars love.

name: Sfizio
hours: Wed-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-9:30pm; closed Sun-Tue
description: Sfizio (pronounced svee-tsio) is a small, affordable pasta shop at the corner of Claremont and College avenues in Rockridge. Chef-owner Matt Solimano, a Pizzaiolo alumnus, started it as a pandemic pop-up in 2020 and opened the brick-and-mortar in May 2023 after years of sold-out events. The short menu is built around fresh pasta and seasonal vegetables, anchored by a famously inexpensive spaghetti in rich red sauce, with rotating plates such as tagliolini with wild morels or charred carrots with salsa macha. Guests order at a counter lined with cookbooks and plants, with a record player setting the mood. Most seats are held for walk-ins, and to-go orders are taken by phone.

name: Shan Dong
description: Shan Dong has been a cornerstone of Oakland's Chinatown since 1992, a family-run restaurant overseen by Charles Hung that is known for its handmade noodles and dumplings. Passersby can often watch cooks stretching noodles and folding dumpling wrappers behind glass while they wait for a table. Regulars come back for the hand-pulled noodles in sesame paste sauce, pork and cabbage dumplings, and Shan Dong chicken, and the restaurant is reported to turn out around 2,000 dumplings a day. It is a casual, bustling spot that works for big group meals and quick lunches, and it runs a busy takeout operation. Expect lines at peak times.

name: Snail Bar
description: Snail Bar is a small natural wine bar and bottle shop on Shattuck Avenue in Temescal that became one of the East Bay's most talked-about restaurants after chef Andres Giraldo Florez, who is from Colombia, opened it in summer 2021. The wine list is entirely natural, mostly French with Spanish and Californian bottles, and it pairs with a concise, inventive menu of small plates that changes often. The restaurant is recommended in the Michelin Guide and is known for its steak frites and some very good french fries. Florez has since moved to Europe, and in early 2026 chef de cuisine Zachary Breaux took over the kitchen with a new menu. Reservations are available online.

name: Sun Moon Studio
hours: Dinner Thu-Sun; first seating 5-5:30pm, last seating 7:45-8:30pm
description: Sun Moon Studio is an intimate tasting-menu restaurant in a West Oakland studio space on Union Street, opened in 2024 by chefs Alan Hsu and Sarah Cooper. Seating is limited to about a dozen guests at each dinner. The seasonal menu showcases farmers and producers from around the region and is cooked with precise, restrained technique, with Asian influences in dishes such as Dungeness crab with yuzu kosho butter over silken tofu or savory egg tarts topped with salmon roe. Dinner runs about two to two and a half hours, with optional wine and non-alcoholic pairings. The restaurant holds a Michelin star and was named one of Bon Appétit's best new restaurants of 2025. Reservations are required.

savory egg tarts with salmon roe

name: T'chaka a Taste of Haiti
hours: As of Oct 2023: Wed-Sat 11am-3pm and 5pm-9pm; Sun 11am-6pm brunch (may have changed)
description: T'chaka is Oakland's first Haitian restaurant, opened in September 2023 inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland by chef-owner Frantz Felix, who calls himself an ambassador for Haiti. Before T'chaka, Felix ran the Caribbean Spices food truck and a restaurant in San Rafael. The menu is a tour of Haitian comfort food: griot (citrus-marinated fried pork), braised oxtails, saltfish with ackee, crispy akra taro fritters, and the namesake t'chaka, a hearty stew of beans, corn, and salted pork. It serves lunch and dinner on weekdays and a Sunday brunch, with takeout and delivery through online ordering.

name: Teni East Kitchen
hours: Piedmont Ave: Mon-Fri 11am-3pm and 5pm-9pm; Sat 11am-9pm; Sun 11am-8:30pm (per official site)
description: Teni East Kitchen is chef-owner Tiyo Shibabaw's Burmese restaurant, now in a larger home on Piedmont Avenue after moving about half a mile from its original Broadway location in 2026. Shibabaw spent a decade at Burma Superstar before striking out on her own, and her cooking pairs Southeast Asian herbs and spices with bright California produce. Favorites include tea leaf salad made with kale, crispy fried whole fish, coconut chicken, chickpea tofu with coconut garlic chili sauce, and Teni's spicy noodles. The Michelin Guide has awarded the restaurant a Bib Gourmand. The Piedmont Avenue space adds a full dining room and full bar, with lunch and dinner daily, plus catering and online ordering.

name: The Cook and Her Farmer
hours: Mon 11am-4pm; Tue-Thu 11am-8pm; Fri-Sat 10am-8pm; closed Sun (per Swan's Market)
description: The Cook and Her Farmer is an all-day cafe, oyster bar, and wine bar inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland. Co-owners Romney Steele, a cookbook author whose family founded Big Sur's Nepenthe, and Steven Day met while farming oysters in Tomales Bay. When that farm closed in 2012 they started running pop-ups, and in 2014 they opened this permanent counter. The cooking is coastal with a Southern touch: fresh-shucked oysters, seasonal plates built on produce from local organic farms, and a list of biodynamic and natural wines. It is a relaxed stop for lunch, an early dinner, or oysters and a glass of wine, and it has hosted live music events.

name: The Fat Lady Bar & Restaurant
hours: Tue-Thu 11:30am-9:30pm; Fri 11:30am-11pm; Sat 5pm-11pm; closed Sun-Mon (per official site)
description: The Fat Lady has poured drinks near Jack London Square since May 1970, when Louis Shaterian set out to bring a little bit of San Francisco to Oakland. It occupies an 1862 building that local lore says once housed a brothel. Inside are a cross-cut oak back bar, warm amber lighting, and beveled glass doors with Art Nouveau brass handles, and a covered, heated patio sits out back. Patricia Shaterian-Rossi and Jerry Rossi have run the restaurant since 1980, and the family is now in its third generation there. The American menu covers the Fat Lady burger with onion strings, flat iron steak with bordelaise, ribeye, seafood linguini, and salmon, and the happy hour is well known. Reservations are available.

name: The Hatch Oakland
hours: Tue-Wed 4pm-11:30pm; Thu 4pm-1am; Fri-Sat 4pm-2am; closed Sun-Mon (per EatOkra; verify)
description: The Hatch is a downtown Oakland bar and gastropub on 15th Street, founded in 2014 by Pancho Kachingwe to serve the neighborhood's growing community. Kachingwe started out cooking, bartending, and cleaning by himself, and the business grew quickly enough to triple its capacity with help from a small-business loan. The Hatch describes itself as a place for cocktails and late-night food, and it stays open until 2 a.m. on weekends. Its founder sees it as a community space first and has opened it to nonprofits and local events. EatOkra lists it as Black-owned. It is a laid-back option for after-work drinks, a late bite, or a night out downtown.

name: The Monk's Kettle
hours: Daily 11:30am-12am (lunch until 4pm, dinner 4-10pm, late night 10pm-close)
description: The Monk's Kettle spent more than sixteen years as a Mission District craft-beer destination before founders Christian Albertson and Nat Cutler moved it across the bay to Rockridge in fall 2024. The College Avenue home, formerly Citron, has a long bar, a dining room and an outdoor deck. The draft and bottle list leans toward Belgian and European styles, with a strong sour selection, and the kitchen serves substantial gastropub plates: the house-ground Monk's Burger with onion jam and gruyere, steak frites, a crisp bricked chicken thigh with gochujang slaw, and a miso-glazed lamb shank at dinner. It is open daily from lunch through late night, with a kids' menu and private event bookings.

name: The Saap Avenue
hours: Sun-Thu 4-9:30pm; Fri-Sat 4-10pm; happy hour daily 4-7pm
description: The Saap Avenue is a family-run Lao restaurant on Piedmont Avenue. Thomas Manyvong opened it in September 2017, with his mother Julie leading the kitchen. The family also runs the Chai Thai Noodles restaurants. It opened as Chai Thai Bar, but within a week it was renamed for its real focus, since saap means delicious in Lao. The menu is built for sharing: Lao papaya salad with padaek, crispy wings with jeow dipping sauce, catfish steamed in banana leaf, fried quail, noodle dishes and curries, plus handcrafted cocktails. Dinner is served nightly with a daily early-evening happy hour, and the restaurant offers reservations, takeout, delivery and catering.
tags: ho mok pla (catfish in banana leaf)

name: The Salty Pearl
hours: Thu-Mon; weekdays 5-9pm, weekends 12-9pm (per official site)
description: The Salty Pearl is a small oyster bar near the water in Jack London Square. Owner Danny Pirello opened it in January 2024 after his earlier restaurant, Rocky Island Oyster Co., lost its home on the Richmond waterfront. The menu centers on freshly shucked oysters from the East and West Coasts, alongside Italian-style crudo, shrimp cocktail, clams casino and a few heartier plates, all paired with a curated wine list. Pirello pictured it as a cozier, date-night version of his Richmond spot. A standing promotion adds a dozen dollar oysters with a bottle of wine on select days. Reservations are taken through OpenTable, and walk-ins are welcome.

name: The Saucy Hut
hours: Tue-Thu 12-8pm; Fri-Sat 12-10pm; Sun 12-8pm; closed Mon (per Toast ordering page)
description: The Saucy Hut began as a food truck and opened its first brick-and-mortar restaurant on Fruitvale Avenue in early 2025, in the space once occupied by La Perla. The menu is short, generous and built around its signature Saucy Sauce. It is best known for egg rolls, including cheesesteak and crab-and-shrimp versions, along with loaded fries, steak rice bowls, steak hoagies and lemon pepper wings. For groups, the Saucy Box combo bundles several favorites. It is a casual counter-style spot for takeout or a quick meal, and online ordering and delivery are available for anyone eating at home.

name: The Wolf
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm; dinner Sun-Wed 5-9pm, Thu-Sat 5-10pm; bar Mon-Fri from 11:30am, Sat-Sun from 4pm (per OpenTable)
description: The Wolf occupies the Craftsman house on Piedmont Avenue that was home to Bay Wolf, Michael Wild's farm-to-table pioneer, from 1975 until 2015. Rich and Rebekah Wood, the couple behind Wood Tavern and Southie, took over and renovated the space and reopened it in 2017. The kitchen is led by executive chef Yang Peng. Seasonal French-Californian cooking is inspired by Oakland's many cultures, and wines are offered by the glass or bottle. A mural by local artist Steven Anderson decorates the building, and there is terrace dining and private event space. It serves weekday lunch and nightly dinner, and the bar stays open between services.
tags: wine by the glass and bottle

name: To The Moon
hours: Nightly approx. 6pm-2am (per Wanderlog; verify)
description: To The Moon is a Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in Temescal, open until 2am and a favorite for a late meal. The menu mixes Korean bar snacks with heartier comfort dishes: crispy Korean fried wings, bubbling corn cheese, tteokbokki, seafood pancake, spicy stir-fried pork and green onion pork belly, plus hot pots, ramen, bibimbap, beef noodle soup and short rib soup. Many dishes follow a simple tiered pricing scheme. The freshly renovated room is relaxed and low-key, which suits groups sharing plates after a night out. Takeout and delivery are also available.

name: Town Fare by Chef Michele McQueen
hours: Wed-Sat 11am-5pm; Sun 11am-4pm (brunch)
description: Town Fare is the cafe inside the Oakland Museum of California. Oakland native Michele McQueen has run it since July 2022, when she took over from Tanya Holland. McQueen studied business at Howard University and made her name with fried chicken and sweet potato waffles at Gussie's Chicken and Waffles in San Francisco. She has also appeared on several Food Network shows. Her menu mixes Southern roots with Oakland's many cultures. Alongside the signature chicken and waffles with house-made syrup, it offers mac and cheese, a smash burger, gumbo ramen, fried chicken bao and a collard green salad. The bright, glass-walled cafe serves lunch, a Sunday brunch, cocktails and local beer, and also caters.

name: Twinflame
hours: Wed, Thu, Sun 5-9pm (last seating 8:15pm); Fri-Sat 5-10pm (last seating 9:15pm); closed Mon-Tue
description: Twinflame is a Korean-Japanese restaurant on the ground floor of the One Piedmont building on West MacArthur Boulevard, near the foot of Piedmont Avenue. The room is modern and industrial, and counter seating wraps around two charcoal robata grills, so diners watch the cooking up close. The short menu is built around Japanese-style hamburg steak charred over charcoal and served as a set with rice and miso soup. Grilled tofu and Korean dishes, soups and noodles round it out. A small bar pours Japanese whisky highballs, wine and beer. It is open for dinner Wednesday through Sunday, with reservations released two weeks ahead and a limited number of walk-in seats.

name: Understory Oakland
hours: Cafe Tue-Fri 9am-2pm; dinner Wed-Fri 5-9pm; brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3pm (as of 2025 reopening coverage)
description: Understory is a worker-owned, queer- and POC-owned restaurant collective. Lily Fahsi-Haskell, Jenabi Pareja, Nino Serrano and Florencio Esquivel founded it in 2020 to support restaurant workers of color during the pandemic. The collective won a James Beard Foundation leadership award for its model. After closing its Old Oakland location in June 2024, it reopened in spring 2025 in a larger space on International Boulevard in Fruitvale, with room for community events and a small art gallery. The Filipino-rooted menu includes favorites such as fried oyster mushrooms, vegan and gluten-free ube waffles, and a caramelized papaya burger. It serves cafe hours on weekdays, dinner midweek and weekend brunch, and no one is turned away for lack of funds.

name: Wahpepah's Kitchen
hours: Wed-Sun 11am-2pm; closed Mon-Tue (per Visit Oakland; verify)
description: Wahpepah's Kitchen is an Indigenous restaurant in Fruitvale Village, steps from the Fruitvale BART station. Chef Crystal Wahpepah, an enrolled member of the Kickapoo Nation who grew up in East Oakland, opened it in November 2021 after more than a decade running a Native catering company. She was the first Native American chef to compete on Food Network's Chopped and is a James Beard Emerging Chef finalist. Her seasonal menu draws on intertribal traditions and Indigenous sources, with dishes such as wild rice cakes, blue corn waffles with turkey wing and berry compote, three-bean bison chili and hominy with squash. Murals by Native artists fill the space, and her cookbook, A Feather and a Fork, was published in 2026.

name: Willows & Pine
hours: Wed-Sun 11am-3pm and 5-9pm (per official site)
description: Willows & Pine is a Louisiana-style soul food restaurant that Michauxnee Olier opened on Fruitvale Avenue in October 2023. It draws on four generations of family history. Olier's great-grandparents came to Oakland from Shreveport and ran The Barn, a West Oakland soul food spot that drew touring performers in the 1950s before redevelopment displaced the neighborhood. Today the kitchen cooks everything to order: shrimp and crawfish chowder, etouffee, jambalaya with shrimp, chicken and sausage, braised oxtails, short ribs and mac and cheese. The family motto, 'real love, no charge,' shapes the hospitality. The restaurant serves daytime and dinner hours Wednesday through Sunday and caters events.

name: Wood Tavern
description: Wood Tavern has been a neighborhood gathering place on College Avenue in Rockridge for two decades. Rich and Rebekah Wood, who previously worked at Rubicon and Farallon in San Francisco, opened the roughly 50-seat brasserie to serve polished California-American cooking in a warm, bustling room where regulars celebrate birthdays and anniversaries. The butcher-block charcuterie, including pork rillettes seasoned with Aleppo pepper, sumac and lime, has drawn Michelin Guide attention. The couple also runs Southie, the sandwich shop next door, and The Wolf on Piedmont Avenue. They have announced that Wood Tavern will close at the end of 2026 when its lease runs out, so there is limited time left to visit.

name: Yellow Door
hours: Wed-Sun 8am-2pm; closed Mon-Tue
description: Yellow Door is a neighborhood cafe in Montclair, easy to spot by the bright yellow door that gives it its name. Longtime friends Beth Barrett and Virginia Davis opened it in 2020 because they wanted a gathering place in the village they loved, pairing good coffee with baked goods made from scratch. The pastry case holds scones, muffins, coffee cakes and cookies, and the cafe has become a regular morning stop for locals and visitors to the hills. It keeps morning and early-afternoon hours Wednesday through Sunday and suits an unhurried coffee and treat or a quick stop on the way up Moraga Avenue.
